meta.provenance: Authored from model knowledge (cutoff Jan 2026). Original explanations — not copied from documentation. Shortcuts/menus are factual data. Run scripts/command-scrapers/scrape-rhino9.mjs to sync names/icons with the live Rhino 9 command list.
meta.iconNote: Icons filled by scraper into rhino9-icons manifest; app serves via /api/v1/rhino-asset/.

commands.name: 3DFace
commands.description: Draws a single mesh face by picking three or four corner points. Handy for patching an individual hole in a mesh or building simple mesh geometry point by point, much like the old AutoCAD workflow.

commands.name: 3View
commands.description: Splits the screen into a three-viewport arrangement instead of the usual four. Useful when you want a large perspective view alongside a couple of orthographic views without the clutter of a full grid.

commands.name: 4View
commands.description: Restores the classic four-viewport arrangement of Top, Front, Right and Perspective. Quick reset when viewport layouts get into a muddle.

commands.name: About
commands.description: Opens the About Rhino dialog showing the exact version, service release and licence details. Reach for it when reporting a bug or checking whether you are on the latest service release.

commands.name: AcadSchemes
commands.description: Manages the export schemes used when saving to AutoCAD formats (DWG/DXF). Set up a scheme once — how curves, layers and hatches translate — then reuse it every time you issue drawings to consultants.

commands.name: AddGuide
commands.description: Places an infinite construction guide line that object snaps recognise but that never prints or exports. Ideal for setting out temporary alignment lines while modelling, without polluting the file with real geometry.

commands.name: AddMissingBlockAttributeKeys
commands.description: Brings block instances up to date so they all carry the full set of attribute keys defined for the block, adding any that are missing. Useful housekeeping when a block definition has gained new data fields after instances were placed.

commands.name: AddNextU
commands.description: Grows the current control-point selection by one point in the surface's U direction. Part of the family of selection helpers that make it quick to grab rows of control points for shaping surfaces.

commands.name: AddNextV
commands.description: Grows the current control-point selection by one point in the surface's V direction. Used with the other row-selection helpers when sculpting surfaces via their control points.

commands.name: AddNgonsToMesh
commands.description: Groups coplanar triangles and quads in a mesh into larger n-sided faces (ngons), giving a cleaner-looking mesh without changing its shape. Useful before exporting to software that prefers ngon meshes, or simply to tidy the wireframe display.

commands.name: AddObjectsToBlock
commands.description: Adds selected geometry to an existing block definition, updating every instance of that block in the model. Saves redefining a block from scratch when a component design gains an extra part.

commands.name: AddPrevU
commands.description: Extends the current control-point selection by one point in the opposite U direction. A quick way to walk a selection along a surface row while fine-tuning form.

commands.name: AddPrevV
commands.description: Extends the current control-point selection by one point in the opposite V direction. Companion to AddNextV for stepping a selection along a surface column.

commands.name: AddToGroup
commands.description: Adds extra objects into an existing group without rebuilding it. Keeps evolving assemblies tidy as elements are added.

commands.name: Alerter
commands.description: Plays a notification sound when a long-running operation finishes, so you can get on with something else while Rhino churns through a heavy calculation or render mesh. Configure the delay threshold and sound to taste.

commands.name: Align
commands.description: Lines up selected objects by their edges or centres, vertically or horizontally. Tidies drawing layouts and rows of objects without manual snapping.

commands.name: AlignVertices
commands.description: Snaps mesh or SubD vertices that sit within a tolerance of each other onto the same location, so nearly-touching edges can then be welded or joined cleanly. A standard first step when repairing meshes with hairline gaps.

commands.name: Angle
commands.description: Measures the angle between two lines or defined directions. Companion to Distance for checking splays and slopes.

commands.name: AppendFace
commands.description: Adds new faces onto existing SubD or mesh edges by picking corner points. Used to grow a form outwards face by face during freeform modelling.

commands.name: ApplyBoxMapping
commands.description: Wraps a texture onto an object by projecting it from the six sides of a box. The go-to mapping for orthogonal, building-like forms where you want materials such as brick or timber to read correctly on every face.

commands.name: ApplyCrv
commands.description: Takes flat curves drawn in the world XY plane and wraps them onto a target surface using the surface's UV parameterisation. Designers use it to lay out patterns, engraving or panel lines flat, then transfer them onto a curved form.

commands.name: ApplyCustomMapping
commands.description: Assigns a custom texture-mapping channel to an object, using another object or a custom widget to control how the texture flows across it. For the cases where the standard planar, box, cylindrical and spherical projections cannot follow the form.

commands.name: ApplyCylindricalMapping
commands.description: Projects a texture onto an object from a surrounding cylinder — the natural choice for columns, tubes, bottles and other rotationally shaped objects where a planar projection would smear.

commands.name: ApplyMesh
commands.description: Deforms a mesh drawn flat in the XY plane onto a target surface via the surface's UV space — the mesh equivalent of ApplyCrv. Useful for wrapping panelisation or relief patterns onto doubly curved surfaces.

commands.name: ApplyMeshUVN
commands.description: Wraps a flat mesh onto a surface using UVN coordinates, where the mesh's height above the flat plane becomes an offset along the surface normal. This lets a flat relief pattern gain genuine depth when transferred to a curved surface.

commands.name: ApplyPlanarMapping
commands.description: Projects a texture flat onto an object from a single plane. The simplest mapping type — right for facades, floors and other broadly flat geometry where you want direct control of texture direction and scale.

commands.name: ApplySphericalMapping
commands.description: Wraps a texture around an object from an enclosing sphere. Suits domes, globes and rounded forms where cylindrical or planar projections would distort at the poles of the shape.

commands.name: ApplySurfaceMapping
commands.description: Uses a separate surface as the mapping object, so the texture follows that surface's UV flow rather than a simple projection. Powerful when you need a texture to track a sweeping, doubly curved form precisely.

commands.name: Arc
commands.description: Draws a circular arc from a centre, start and angle, with options for tangent and other constructions. Everyday tool for door swings, filleted corners drawn manually and curved wall segments.

commands.name: Arc3Pt
commands.description: Draws an arc through three picked points. Quick when you know where the arc starts, ends and passes, but not its centre or radius.

commands.name: ArcBlend
commands.description: Bridges two curves with a pair of tangent arcs you can adjust interactively. A quick alternative to BlendCrv when arc-based geometry is preferred for fabrication.

commands.name: Area
commands.description: Calculates the area of closed curves, hatches, surfaces or meshes. Constantly used for schedules of accommodation and material take-offs.

commands.name: AreaCentroid
commands.description: Calculates area and marks the centroid with a point. Useful for balance points in structural sketches and for centring elements within outlines.

commands.name: AreaMoments
commands.description: Calculates area moments of inertia, centroid and related section properties for closed planar curves, hatches or surfaces. Structural-minded designers use it to check section stiffness properties of a profile before handing it to an engineer.

commands.name: Array
commands.description: Copies objects into a rectangular grid with set counts and spacing in X, Y and Z. The base tool for column grids, seating layouts and repeated bays.

commands.name: ArrayCrv
commands.description: Copies objects along a curve by count or spacing, optionally rotating them to follow it. Perfect for balustrades, ribs and streetlights along a curved route.

commands.name: ArrayCrvOnSrf
commands.description: Copies objects along a curve that lies on a surface, keeping each copy normal to the surface. Used for fixings or fins that must track a curved seam on a facade.

commands.name: ArrayHole
commands.description: Repeats an existing hole across a face in rows and columns. Efficient for perforated panels and fixing grids once one opening is placed.

commands.name: ArrayHolePolar
commands.description: Takes an existing hole in a planar surface and repeats it in a circular pattern around a centre point. Quicker than re-cutting: think bolt circles, perforated discs or radial ventilation patterns.

commands.name: ArrayLinear
commands.description: Copies objects repeatedly along a single direction at even spacing. Quick for fence posts, joists and any one-directional rhythm.

commands.name: ArrayPolar
commands.description: Copies objects around a centre point through a set angle and count. The go-to for radial structures, stair balusters on a curve and circular seating.

commands.name: ArraySrf
commands.description: Copies an object across a surface in its U and V directions, orienting each copy to the surface normal. The manual panelisation tool for cladding studies and facade components.

commands.name: Arrowhead
commands.description: Adds or removes an arrowhead at the end of a curve, turning plain curves into leader-like graphic arrows. Handy for annotating diagrams and presentation drawings without building full leader annotations.

commands.name: AttachGHSData
commands.description: Attaches GHS (General HydroStatics) metadata to geometry so hull and compartment models can be exported for naval-architecture stability analysis. Specialist marine tooling — most designers will never need it.

commands.name: Audit
commands.description: Checks the open model's database for errors and reports what it finds. Run with Purge and SaveSmall as a standard file hygiene routine.

commands.name: Audit3dmFile
commands.description: Reads a 3dm file from disk and reports its internal structure, tables and any damage, without fully opening it. The first diagnostic to run on a file that refuses to open or behaves strangely.

commands.name: AutoAlignCPlane
commands.description: Toggles automatic construction-plane alignment, so the CPlane snaps itself to the surface or object under your cursor as you work. Speeds up modelling on angled faces without constantly running CPlane commands by hand.

commands.name: AutoCPlane
commands.description: Automatically aligns the construction plane to whatever object or face you select. A Rhino 8 quality-of-life tool that removes constant manual CPlane setting when detailing angled geometry.

commands.name: Autosave
commands.description: Saves the current model to Rhino's autosave file immediately, on demand. A belt-and-braces save before attempting something risky, separate from your named file on disk.

commands.name: BackgroundBitmap
commands.description: Places, scales and manages a reference image behind the geometry in a single viewport — the traditional way to trace over a scanned sketch, plan or photograph. Largely superseded by Picture objects, but still useful for per-viewport tracing.

commands.name: Bake
commands.description: Converts procedural textures on an object's material into ordinary bitmap textures. Run it before exporting to software that cannot evaluate Rhino's procedural noise, gradient or tile textures.

commands.name: BatchRenderNamedViews
commands.description: Renders every (or a chosen set of) named views one after another and saves the images to disk. Set up your camera angles as named views, start the batch, and come back to a full set of presentation renders.

commands.name: Bend
commands.description: Bends objects along a spine between two points, with control over the arc. Useful for curving straight elements like trusses or louvres through an angle.

commands.name: Bevel
commands.description: Replaces selected SubD edges or vertices with narrow face strips, hardening the corner while staying smooth. The SubD equivalent of a fillet for controlling edge tightness.

commands.name: BlendCrv
commands.description: Creates an adjustable smooth connecting curve between two curve ends, with control over continuity up to curvature and beyond. Reach for it when a plain fillet looks too mechanical.

commands.name: BlendEdge
commands.description: Rounds solid edges with a curvature-continuous blend rather than a plain circular fillet. Chosen when reflections must flow uninterrupted across an edge, as on visible ceiling or furniture pieces.

commands.name: BlendSrf
commands.description: Creates a smooth transition surface between two surface edges with adjustable continuity and shape handles. The refined option for junctions where FilletSrf feels too rigid.

commands.name: Block
commands.description: Defines selected geometry as a named block so copies insert as lightweight linked instances. Editing the definition updates every instance, ideal for repeated windows, furniture and units.

commands.name: BlockEdit
commands.description: Opens a block definition for editing in place, with surrounding context shown. Changes propagate to every instance on exit, keeping repeated elements consistent.

commands.name: BlockManager
commands.description: Lists every block definition in the file with counts, links and update controls. The housekeeping hub for models built on components and externally referenced files.

commands.name: Boolean2Objects
commands.description: Cycles interactively through all boolean outcomes of two objects until you see the one you want. A forgiving way to run booleans without remembering which operand order to pick.

commands.name: BooleanDifference
commands.description: Subtracts one set of solids from another, cutting openings and voids. Constantly used for door and window openings, service penetrations and courtyard cuts.

commands.name: BooleanIntersection
commands.description: Keeps only the volume shared by two sets of solids. Useful for finding overlap zones, clash volumes and sculpting forms from intersecting masses.

commands.name: BooleanSplit
commands.description: Splits solids into separate closed pieces along their shared intersections, keeping everything. Great for dividing a massing model into phases or storeys while retaining all parts.

commands.name: BooleanUnion
commands.description: Merges overlapping solids into one, removing internal walls. The standard way to consolidate massing elements into a single clean volume.

commands.name: Boss
commands.description: Extrudes closed planar profile curves up to a surface on a solid and unions the result, creating a raised boss feature in one step. A quick way to add pads and protrusions to a part without manual extrusion and boolean work.

commands.name: Bounce
commands.description: Fires a ray from a start point and direction, reflecting it off surfaces a set number of times to produce a polyline of the bounce path. Useful for quick acoustic or daylight reflection studies inside a space.

commands.name: BoundingBox
commands.description: Draws the smallest world- or CPlane-aligned box enclosing the selection. Handy for overall envelope dimensions, crate sizing and stock material checks.

commands.name: Box
commands.description: Creates a rectangular solid box from corners or centre. The first tool most designers reach for in massing studies and quick spatial blocking.

commands.name: BoxEdit
commands.description: Opens a panel for numerically transforming objects via their bounding box — exact position, size and rotation typed in rather than dragged. Invaluable when objects must be a precise overall dimension or sit at exact coordinates.

commands.name: Bridge
commands.description: Connects two SubD or mesh face groups or edge loops with a smooth linking tunnel. Used to join limbs, create handles and punch connected openings through sculpted forms.

commands.name: BringForward
commands.description: Moves a curve, hatch or other 2D element one step up in the draw order, so it displays in front of the object it was behind. Part of the draw-order tools used to compose layered 2D drawings.

commands.name: BringToFront
commands.description: Puts the selected curves, hatches or annotations at the very top of the draw order so they display in front of everything else. Essential when composing 2D drawings where hatches keep hiding your linework.

commands.name: BringViewportToTop
commands.description: Makes a named viewport the active, frontmost one — mostly useful in scripts and button macros that need to guarantee which viewport subsequent commands act on.

commands.name: Cage
commands.description: Creates a standalone box, line or surface cage object for later use with CageEdit. Set up once, then reuse across multiple deformation studies.

commands.name: CageEdit
commands.description: Surrounds objects with a low-point control cage and deforms them by moving its points. The heavyweight freeform editor for reshaping whole buildings or complex assemblies smoothly.

commands.name: Calc
commands.description: Pops up an on-screen calculator whose result can be fed straight into the command line. Saves reaching for a separate calculator when a dimension needs working out mid-command.

commands.name: CalcRPN
commands.description: Opens a Reverse Polish Notation calculator, for those who prefer HP-style stack entry, with results usable directly in the command line. Same job as Calc, different keystroke philosophy.

commands.name: Camera
commands.description: Shows or hides the active view's camera widget so its position, target and lens can be manipulated as objects. Used to fine-tune verified views and match photographs.

commands.name: Cancel
commands.description: Cancels the running command, exactly like pressing Escape. Exists mainly so button macros and scripts can bail out of whatever state Rhino is in before starting fresh.

commands.name: Cap
commands.description: Closes planar openings in a surface or polysurface with flat faces, making it a closed solid. The usual fix after extruding or trimming leaves an open top or bottom.

commands.name: Catenary
commands.description: Draws a true catenary — the curve a chain takes hanging under its own weight — between two points, with control over length or sag. A gift for architects working on hanging chains, arches, tents and gridshell form-finding sketches.

commands.name: Centermark
commands.description: Places a centre cross on an arc or circle. Small but essential drafting mark for setting out circular elements.

commands.name: Chamfer
commands.description: Connects two curves with an angled straight segment at set distances, trimming them to suit. Used for bevelled corners on frames, plates and joinery profiles.

commands.name: ChamferEdge
commands.description: Bevels selected solid edges with a flat strip at set distances. Used for arris details, machined looks and edge easing on precast elements.

commands.name: ChamferSrf
commands.description: Connects two surfaces with a flat angled strip at set distances, trimming both back. Suits bevelled edges on plinths, frames and machined-looking details.

commands.name: ChangeDegree
commands.description: Raises or lowers the polynomial degree of a curve or surface, adding or reducing flexibility. Used when geometry needs more subtle shaping or simpler structure for matching.

commands.name: ChangeLayer
commands.description: Moves selected objects onto a different layer chosen from a list. Quicker than the properties panel for bulk re-layering during clean-ups.

commands.name: ChangeSpace
commands.description: Moves objects between model space and a layout's paper space (or between layouts), converting their geometry to suit the destination. Useful when notes or drawing graphics were made in the wrong space.

commands.name: ChangeToCurrentLayer
commands.description: Moves the selected objects onto whichever layer is current. One of the fastest layer-tidying moves: set the layer you want, select strays, run the command.

commands.name: Check
commands.description: Tests selected objects for internal errors and reports whether they are valid. Routine health check before booleans, exports and file handovers.

commands.name: CheckInLicense
commands.description: Returns a checked-out Rhino licence to the team's licence server (Zoo or Cloud Zoo) so someone else can use it. Pair of CheckOutLicense for laptop users who roam between office and site.

commands.name: CheckNewObjects
commands.description: Toggles automatic checking of every newly created or imported object for geometry errors, warning the moment a bad object appears. Slower, but invaluable for tracing exactly which operation is producing invalid geometry.

commands.name: CheckOutLicense
commands.description: Borrows a licence from the team's licence server so Rhino keeps working while you are offline — on site, on a plane, at home. Check it back in when you return so colleagues aren't locked out.

commands.name: Circle
commands.description: Draws a circle from centre and radius, with vertical, tangent and other placement options. Fundamental for columns, service penetrations and construction geometry.

commands.name: Circle3Pt
commands.description: Draws a circle through three picked points. Useful for reconstructing circles from surveyed or traced positions where the centre is unknown.

commands.name: Clash
commands.description: Runs clash detection between two sets of objects, reporting where they intersect or come within a given clearance. Architects use it to check services against structure, or a design against a site constraint envelope.

commands.name: ClearAllMeshes
commands.description: Deletes the render and analysis meshes cached in the file for all surfaces and solids, often shrinking the file dramatically before saving or sending. The meshes regenerate automatically next time a shaded view needs them.

commands.name: ClearAllObjectDisplayModes
commands.description: Removes every per-object display-mode override in the model, returning all objects to the viewport's own display mode. The quick undo for a model peppered with SetObjectDisplayMode experiments.

commands.name: ClearAnalysisMeshes
commands.description: Deletes the extra-fine meshes created for curvature, draft-angle and similar visual analyses. Frees memory and file size once you have finished analysing.

commands.name: ClearDrawOrder
commands.description: Resets the draw order of selected 2D elements back to the default, discarding any BringToFront and SendToBack arrangements. Use it when a drawing's stacking has become impossible to reason about.

commands.name: ClearUndo
commands.description: Empties the undo buffer, releasing the memory it holds. Worth running after huge operations on big models when Rhino is getting sluggish — but be certain you no longer need to undo anything.

commands.name: ClippingPlane
commands.description: Places a plane that cuts the viewport display away on one side, revealing a live section. Invaluable for working inside buildings and presenting sectional 3D views.

commands.name: CloseCrv
commands.description: Closes an open curve either with a straight segment or by adjusting the curve to meet itself. Needed before extruding or building planar surfaces that require closed boundaries.

commands.name: CloseRenderWindow
commands.description: Closes the render window. Exists mostly so scripts and batch workflows can tidy up after saving a render.

commands.name: ClosestPt
commands.description: Finds and marks the closest point on an object from a test point, or the closest points between objects. Useful for measuring minimum clearances and for locating exact contact points before dimensioning.

commands.name: CloseViewport
commands.description: Closes the active viewport, removing it from the layout of views. Used with NewViewport and floating viewports to customise the workspace.

commands.name: CollapseMeshEdge
commands.description: Collapses a mesh edge to a single vertex, merging its two end vertices and removing the faces that depended on it. A precise, surgical tool for reducing or repairing meshes one edge at a time.

commands.name: CollapseMeshFace
commands.description: Collapses a whole mesh face down to a single vertex, welding its corners together. Useful for eliminating awkward slivers and pinch points during manual mesh repair.

commands.name: CollapseMeshFacesByArea
commands.description: Collapses every mesh face whose area falls below (or within) a threshold you set, removing insignificant faces in one pass. A batch clean-up for scan data and imported meshes littered with tiny faces.

commands.name: CollapseMeshFacesByAspectRatio
commands.description: Collapses mesh faces whose aspect ratio exceeds a threshold — the long, thin slivers that cause shading artefacts and break downstream tools. Batch companion to the one-at-a-time collapse commands.

commands.name: CollapseMeshFacesByEdgeLength
commands.description: Collapses mesh faces that have edges shorter (or longer) than a length you specify. Another of the criteria-based batch tools for thinning out problem faces in heavy or messy meshes.

commands.name: CollapseMeshVertex
commands.description: Merges a chosen mesh vertex into an adjacent one, removing the edge between them. The finest-grained of the collapse tools for hand-editing mesh topology.

commands.name: CommandHelp
commands.description: Opens the help panel showing documentation for whichever command is running or last ran, updating as you work. Keep it docked while learning and Rhino effectively narrates itself.

commands.name: CommandHistory
commands.description: Opens the scrolling log of recent commands and their reported results. Where you retrieve measurement outputs and diagnose what a command actually did.

commands.name: CommandList
commands.description: Displays a browsable list of every command available in this Rhino installation, including those added by plug-ins. A good way to discover tools you did not know existed.

commands.name: CommandPrompt
commands.description: Controls where the command prompt lives — shown, hidden, docked top or bottom, or floating. Purely a workspace preference, but a vital one to know when the prompt vanishes.

commands.name: ComputeVertexColors
commands.description: Evaluates the texture applied to a mesh and stores the resulting colours directly on the mesh's vertices. Used to carry colour into formats and workflows (3D printing, some viewers) that support vertex colour but not textures.

commands.name: Cone
commands.description: Creates a solid cone from a base and apex. Useful for roof forms, funnels and transitional volumes.

commands.name: Conic
commands.description: Draws a conic section curve controlled by end points, a shoulder and a rho value. Valued in industrial and facade design for tight, mathematically clean transition curves.

commands.name: Connect
commands.description: Extends or trims two curves so their ends meet exactly. Fast tidy-up for drafting where lines overshoot or fall short of a corner.

commands.name: ConnectSrf
commands.description: Extends and/or trims two surfaces so their edges meet cleanly along a shared boundary — the surface counterpart of Connect for curves. Saves the extend-intersect-trim dance when squaring up construction surfaces.

commands.name: ContinueCurve
commands.description: Picks up an existing control-point curve at its end and lets you keep placing control points as if you had never stopped. Better than drawing a new curve and joining, because the result stays one smooth curve.

commands.name: ContinueInterpCrv
commands.description: Continues an existing interpolated curve by adding further through-points from its end. The interpolated-curve twin of ContinueCurve, keeping the extended result a single clean curve.

commands.name: Contour
commands.description: Cuts a stack of evenly spaced section curves through objects along an axis. The classic tool for site contours, waffle structures and laser-cut sectional models.

commands.name: Convert
commands.description: Rebuilds curves as sequences of lines and arcs (or polylines) within a tolerance. Essential preparation for CNC cutting, laser profiles and export to software that only understands arcs and lines.

commands.name: ConvertDots
commands.description: Turns annotation dots into text objects or point objects (and can carry the dot text across). Useful when survey or coordination data arrives as dots but you need editable text or plain points.

commands.name: ConvertExtrusion
commands.description: Converts lightweight extrusion objects into ordinary surfaces and polysurfaces so their full editing toolset becomes available. Run it when a command refuses to work on what looks like a normal box or cylinder.

commands.name: ConvertTextToBlockAttribute
commands.description: Converts a text object inside a block into an attribute, so each instance of the block can display its own value — think room tags, door numbers, titleblock fields. Key to building data-aware blocks.

commands.name: ConvertToBeziers
commands.description: Splits curves and surfaces into their constituent single-span Bezier pieces. Occasionally needed for export to systems that only accept Bezier geometry, or for low-level surface analysis.

commands.name: Copy
commands.description: Duplicates objects from a base point to one or more target points. The everyday tool for repeating elements around a drawing with precision.

commands.name: CopyCPlaneSettingsToAll
commands.description: Copies the active viewport's construction-plane settings — grid spacing, snap, extents — to every other viewport. Keeps the workspace consistent after tuning one viewport's grid.

commands.name: CopyCPlaneToAll
commands.description: Applies the active viewport's construction plane to all viewports at once. Useful when working on an angled datum — set the CPlane once, and every view shares it.

commands.name: CopyDetailToViewport
commands.description: Copies the camera and view settings of a layout detail into a model-space viewport, so you can model from exactly the view a drawing shows. The reverse of CopyViewportToDetail.

commands.name: CopyHole
commands.description: Copies an existing hole in a planar surface to new locations on the same or another planar face. Much faster than re-drawing profiles and re-cutting when a fixing pattern repeats.

commands.name: CopyLayout
commands.description: Duplicates an entire layout page, including its details and title-block graphics. The quickest way to build a drawing set where every sheet shares the same setup.

commands.name: CopyRenderWindowToClipboard
commands.description: Copies the current render window image to the system clipboard, ready to paste into an email, document or image editor. Handy for quick design-review snapshots without saving files.

commands.name: CopyToClipboard
commands.description: Copies the selection to the clipboard without removing it, ready to paste in place or into another file. The quickest way to shuttle geometry between open models.

commands.name: CopyToLayer
commands.description: Copies the selected objects onto another layer, leaving the originals where they are. Ideal for creating option studies or a frozen record copy while continuing to work on the live version.

commands.name: CopyViewportToDetail
commands.description: Creates a layout detail whose camera matches the current model-space viewport. Set up the perfect view while modelling, then drop it straight onto a sheet.

commands.name: CPlane
commands.description: Redefines the construction plane by origin, three points, object or view. Mastering CPlanes is the key to drawing accurately on sloped roofs and angled facades.

commands.name: Crease
commands.description: Makes selected SubD edges or vertices perfectly sharp while the rest stays smooth. Essential for mixing crisp architectural arrises into otherwise soft forms.

commands.name: CreaseSplitting
commands.description: Toggles whether Rhino splits surfaces at kinks (creases) as they are created, or leaves them as single creased surfaces. Advanced modellers switch it off for specific workflows, but split-at-crease is the safer default.

commands.name: CreateSolid
commands.description: Builds closed solids from a set of intersecting surfaces that enclose volumes. Useful late in a workflow when separate walls, roofs and cuts need consolidating into watertight bodies.

commands.name: CreateUniqueBlock
commands.description: Turns the selected block instance into a new, independent block definition, so edits to it no longer affect its siblings. The escape hatch when one repeated element needs to diverge from the rest.

commands.name: CreateUVCrv
commands.description: Lays out a surface's border and trim curves flat in world XY according to its UV parameter space. The first step for designing perforation or graphic patterns that will be flowed back onto the surface.

commands.name: Crv2View
commands.description: Builds a 3D curve from two planar curves drawn in different views, combining the shape seen in one view with the shape seen in the other. Classic technique for modelling handles, hulls and rails defined by plan and elevation profiles.

commands.name: CrvDeviation
commands.description: Reports the minimum and maximum distance between two curves. Useful for checking a simplified curve against its source or clearances between routes.

commands.name: CrvEnd
commands.description: Places a point object at the end of each selected curve. Useful for marking connection points, checking curve direction, or generating snap targets for later operations.

commands.name: CrvSeam
commands.description: Moves the seam point of a closed curve to a new position along it. Fixes twisting in lofts and sweeps caused by mismatched seam locations between profiles.

commands.name: CrvStart
commands.description: Places a point object at the start of each selected curve. A quick visual check of which way curves run — important before lofting, sweeping or flow operations.

commands.name: CSec
commands.description: Creates cross-section profile curves through a set of shape curves, cutting them with a plane you position. Traditional boat- and product-modelling workflow: define a form with a few character curves, then generate the sections to loft through.

commands.name: CullControlPolygon
commands.description: Toggles culling of control points and control polygons that face away from the view, so you only see and select the ones on your side of the object. A sanity-saver when point-editing dense surfaces and SubDs.

commands.name: CullDegenerateMeshFaces
commands.description: Finds and deletes degenerate mesh faces — zero-area slivers whose corners are collinear or coincident. One of the standard passes when repairing imported or scanned meshes for printing or rendering.

commands.name: Curvature
commands.description: Evaluates curvature at a picked point on a curve or surface, reporting the value and optionally placing the osculating circle. The precise, numeric complement to the visual curvature-graph and false-colour analyses.

commands.name: CurvatureAnalysis
commands.description: Shades surfaces with false colour showing Gaussian or mean curvature. Reveals flat spots, dents and double curvature that plain shading hides.

commands.name: CurvatureAnalysisOff
commands.description: Turns off the false-colour curvature analysis display for the selected (or all) objects. Companion switch to CurvatureAnalysis; also exists so macros can end an analysis session cleanly.

commands.name: CurvatureGraph
commands.description: Displays comb-like graphs showing how curvature varies along curves and surface edges. The professional's tool for judging whether a curve is genuinely fair before surfacing.

commands.name: CurvatureGraphOff
commands.description: Removes the curvature-graph display from the selected (or all) curves and surfaces. The off-switch for CurvatureGraph once you have finished checking fairness.

commands.name: Curve
commands.description: Draws a free-form NURBS curve by placing control points that pull the curve towards them. The go-to tool for smooth, editable design curves where flow matters more than hitting exact points.

commands.name: CurveBoolean
commands.description: Trims and joins overlapping closed planar curves by picking the regions to keep, like a 2D boolean. Brilliant for cleaning up overlapping plan outlines into single boundaries.

commands.name: CurveThroughPolyline
commands.description: Fits a smooth NURBS curve through (or controlled by) the vertices of a polyline. The quick route from a faceted survey or GIS polyline to a clean, fair curve.

commands.name: CurveThroughPt
commands.description: Builds a single curve through a set of selected point objects in order. Turns imported survey or grid points into usable design curves in one step.

commands.name: CurveThroughSrfControlPt
commands.description: Creates curves that pass through a surface's rows or columns of control points. Useful for extracting the underlying structure of a surface to rebuild, analyse or re-loft it.

commands.name: Cut
commands.description: Removes the selection and places it on the clipboard for pasting, including into another open Rhino file. Standard clipboard workflow between models.

commands.name: CutPlane
commands.description: Creates flat planes that slice through selected objects at picked locations, sized to cover them. Convenient starting geometry for trimming solids or setting up section cuts.

commands.name: Cylinder
commands.description: Creates a solid cylinder from a base circle and height. Everyday geometry for columns, pipework and circular cores.

commands.name: Delete
commands.description: Removes the selected objects from the model. Paired with the Sel commands for fast bulk clean-ups.

commands.name: DeleteFaces
commands.description: Deletes selected sub-object faces from a polysurface, SubD or mesh, leaving the remainder open. Faster than extracting then deleting when you simply want faces gone — say, removing a glazing face to model into an opening.

commands.name: DeleteMeshFaces
commands.description: Removes picked faces from a mesh, leaving holes. Used to strip unwanted clutter such as scan noise, cars or vegetation from context meshes.

commands.name: DeleteMeshNgons
commands.description: Removes ngon groupings from a mesh, returning it to plain triangles and quads without moving any vertices. The undo for AddNgonsToMesh when downstream software chokes on ngons.

commands.name: DeleteSubCrv
commands.description: Removes the portion of a curve between two points you pick, leaving the rest intact. Cleaner than splitting and deleting when you just need a gap in a curve.

commands.name: Detail
commands.description: Adds and manages viewport windows on a layout page, each with its own view and scale. Used to compose plans, elevations and 3D views on one sheet.

commands.name: DevLoft
commands.description: Creates a developable surface between two rail curves — one that can be unrolled perfectly flat without stretching. Fundamental for sheet-metal, plywood and fabric construction where material cannot deform in-plane.

commands.name: Diameter
commands.description: Reports the diameter of curvature at a picked point on a curve — twice the radius the curve is bending through there. Quick check of whether an arc or curve meets a minimum bend diameter.

commands.name: DigBeep
commands.description: Toggles the confirmation beep a connected 3D digitising arm makes when a point is taken. Small quality-of-life setting for long digitising sessions.

commands.name: DigCalibrate
commands.description: Re-establishes the relationship between a connected digitising arm's coordinate system and the Rhino model, by taking reference points. Run it whenever the physical object or arm has moved.

commands.name: DigDisconnect
commands.description: Disconnects the currently connected 3D digitising arm from Rhino. Housekeeping command at the end of a digitising session.

commands.name: Digitize
commands.description: Connects a 3D digitising arm (MicroScribe, Faro and similar) so its stylus can feed real-world points straight into Rhino commands. The entry point for reverse-engineering physical objects by touch.

commands.name: DigLine
commands.description: Draws line segments from points taken with a connected digitising arm. One of the sketching commands available while a digitizer is driving input.

commands.name: DigPause
commands.description: Temporarily suspends digitizer input so you can use the mouse and keyboard normally, then resume taking points. Practical mid-session control during long digitising work.

commands.name: DigScale
commands.description: Sets a scale factor between the physical object under the digitising arm and the Rhino model, so you can digitise a scale model and receive full-size geometry (or vice versa).

commands.name: DigSection
commands.description: Traces section curves across a physical object using a digitising arm, producing planar profile curves in the model. A staple of hands-on reverse engineering before lofting surfaces through the sections.

commands.name: DigSketch
commands.description: Sketches freehand curves by dragging the stylus of a connected digitising arm across a physical surface. The digitizer equivalent of the Sketch command.

commands.name: Dim
commands.description: Places a horizontal or vertical linear dimension between two points. The bread-and-butter dimensioning tool for plans and elevations.

commands.name: DimAligned
commands.description: Places a dimension parallel to the line between its two picked points. Used for measuring along sloped walls, stairs and raked elements.

commands.name: DimAngle
commands.description: Dimensions the angle between two lines or three points with an arc leader. Standard for splayed walls and angled setting-out.

commands.name: DimArea
commands.description: Places an annotation reporting the area of a closed curve, hatch or surface, and keeps it linked so it updates when the geometry changes. Perfect for room areas and site-area schedules on drawings.

commands.name: DimCurveLength
commands.description: Annotates the true developed length of a curve rather than a straight distance. Useful for handrails, cable runs and curved facades where arc length matters.

commands.name: DimDiameter
commands.description: Annotates the diameter of a circle or arc. Preferred over radius for holes, penetrations and circular components.

commands.name: DimOrdinate
commands.description: Places running X or Y coordinate dimensions from a datum origin. Common on fabrication and setting-out drawings where chains of dimensions would clutter.

commands.name: DimRadius
commands.description: Annotates the radius of an arc or circle with a leadered value. Essential on setting-out drawings for curved kerbs, walls and fillets.

commands.name: DimRecenterText
commands.description: Snaps dimension text that has been dragged around back to its default position on the dimension line. Fast tidy-up for drawings where text has wandered during editing.

commands.name: DimRotated
commands.description: Places a linear dimension at a set angle regardless of the picked points' alignment. Useful for dimensioning against a rotated grid or datum.

commands.name: DimVolume
commands.description: Places an annotation reporting the volume of closed solids, linked so it updates as the model changes. Useful for quick cut-and-fill notes, tank capacities or massing figures directly on a drawing.

commands.name: Dir
commands.description: Displays and edits the direction arrows of curves and the normals of surfaces or meshes. First diagnostic when offsets, extrusions or textures behave back to front.

commands.name: DisableClippingPlane
commands.description: Switches off selected clipping planes in chosen viewports without deleting them, restoring the uncut view. Toggle sections on and off as you flip between design work and section checking.

commands.name: DisableOsnap
commands.description: Temporarily disables all persistent object snaps (or re-enables them), like clicking Disable on the osnap toolbar. Mostly used in macros, or when snaps keep grabbing unwanted points during freehand work.

commands.name: DisplayCommandPrompt
commands.description: Shows or hides the command prompt window. The rescue command to type blind when the prompt has disappeared and Rhino seems unresponsive to instructions.

commands.name: DisplayProperties
commands.description: Opens the display panel for the active viewport, exposing the current display mode's settings for quick adjustment. Faster than digging through Options when you just want to tweak shadows, edges or background.

commands.name: Distance
commands.description: Reports the distance between two picked points. The quickest sanity check on clearances and spacings while modelling.

commands.name: Distribute
commands.description: Spaces selected objects evenly between the outermost ones along an axis. Companion to Align for tidy elevation compositions and furniture rows.

commands.name: Divide
commands.description: Places point objects along a curve by equal count or set length. The standard setting-out tool for mullion spacing, baluster positions and panelisation.

commands.name: DivideAlongCreases
commands.description: Splits a surface into separate faces wherever it kinks at tangency or curvature breaks. Cleans up geometry so downstream fillets, offsets and exports behave predictably.

commands.name: DocumentProperties
commands.description: Opens settings that belong to the current file, such as units, tolerances, grid and annotation styles. Getting tolerances right here prevents most downstream joining and boolean grief.

commands.name: DocumentPropertiesPage
commands.description: Opens the Document Properties dialog directly at a named page — units, grid, mesh settings and so on. Chiefly a scripting and toolbar-button convenience for jumping straight to a settings page.

commands.name: DocumentText
commands.description: Manages document user text — named key/value pairs stored in the file itself, such as project number, revision or client. These fields can drive titleblock text, making them the backbone of consistent drawing sets.

commands.name: DollyZoom
commands.description: Zooms by moving the camera forwards or backwards while simultaneously changing the lens length, keeping the target framed — the cinematic 'vertigo' effect. Useful for tuning perspective drama in a view without losing composition.

commands.name: Domain
commands.description: Reports the parameter domain of a curve or surface — the internal number range over which it is defined. A geometry-nerd utility that matters when scripting or diagnosing parameterisation issues.

commands.name: Dot
commands.description: Places an annotation dot — a small text tag that always faces the camera and stays the same size on screen at any zoom. The go-to markup for labelling, redlining and to-do notes inside a model.

commands.name: DownloadLibraryTextures
commands.description: Fetches the full-resolution textures for Rhino's built-in material library that are not shipped with the installer. Run it once on a new machine so library materials render properly.

commands.name: DraftAngleAnalysis
commands.description: Colours surfaces by their angle from a pull direction. Used to check mould release on cast components and to map facade panels against rain or solar angle thresholds.

commands.name: DraftAngleAnalysisOff
commands.description: Turns off the false-colour draft-angle analysis display. The off-switch once you have finished checking pull directions for moulding, casting or formwork.

commands.name: Drag
commands.description: Sets how click-and-drag moving behaves, including CPlane or view-based dragging. Worth knowing when dragged objects jump to unexpected planes in 3D views.

commands.name: DragMode
commands.description: Sets how objects and control points move when dragged with the mouse — along the construction plane, in world axes, along surface UVN directions, or following the control polygon. Switching drag mode is key to sculpting surfaces and SubDs predictably.

commands.name: DragStrength
commands.description: Scales how far objects and control points actually move relative to your mouse drag, from full strength down to fine fractions. Turn it down for delicate control-point sculpting where full-strength drags are too coarse.

commands.name: Drape
commands.description: Drops a rectangular surface over objects from above, like laying cloth across the model. A quick way to make simplified terrain or wrapper surfaces over complex geometry.

commands.name: DrapePt
commands.description: Drops a rectangular grid of points onto whatever geometry lies below, like draping in points rather than a surface. Useful for sampling terrain or scan data at a regular spacing.

commands.name: DupAnnotationStyle
commands.description: Duplicates an existing annotation (dimension) style as the starting point for a new one. Standard practice for building a family of related drawing styles — copy the office standard, tweak the scale or arrows.

commands.name: DupBorder
commands.description: Duplicates the naked outer edges of a surface, polysurface, mesh or hatch as curves. Fast way to recover an outline for offsetting, trimming or documentation.

commands.name: DupEdge
commands.description: Copies individually picked surface or polysurface edges as free-standing curves. Handy for rebuilding, sweeping or dimensioning from existing geometry.

commands.name: DupFaceBorder
commands.description: Duplicates the full border of a chosen face within a polysurface, including any trim holes. Useful when detailing a single panel of a larger assembly.

commands.name: DupLayer
commands.description: Duplicates a layer, optionally including all the objects on it. Quick way to spin off a design option or archive the current state of one layer before major edits.

commands.name: DupMeshEdge
commands.description: Creates curves that duplicate selected mesh edges. Handy for extracting construction lines from a mesh — a ridge line, a panel joint — to rebuild as clean NURBS geometry.

commands.name: DupMeshHoleBoundary
commands.description: Creates closed polylines around the holes in a mesh. The first step in patching: extract the hole boundaries, then use them to build filling geometry or to see where a scan is incomplete.

commands.name: EarthAnchorPoint
commands.description: Assigns a real-world latitude, longitude and north direction to a point in the model, geolocating it on the planet. Prerequisite for accurate sun studies and for exports that carry geographic position.

commands.name: EdgeContinuity
commands.description: Displays live position, tangency and curvature deviation between two selected edges. A focused matching diagnostic introduced alongside modern surfacing tools in Rhino 7.

commands.name: EdgeSrf
commands.description: Builds a surface spanning two, three or four boundary curves or edges. A dependable way to skin simple openings and quad patches without loft direction fuss.

commands.name: EditLightByHighlight
commands.description: Repositions a light by clicking where you want its highlight to fall on a surface; Rhino moves the light to produce that reflection. An intuitive way to art-direct speculars in product-style renders.

commands.name: EditLightByLooking
commands.description: Aims a light by letting you navigate a viewport as if looking through the light itself — where you point the view is where the light points. The quickest way to aim spotlights precisely at what matters.

commands.name: EditPythonScript
commands.description: Opens Rhino's built-in Python script editor with debugging, so you can write and run Python automation against the live document. The doorway into scripting for anyone automating repetitive modelling or data tasks.

commands.name: EditScript
commands.description: Opens the RhinoScript editor for writing and debugging scripts in Rhino's classic VBScript-based language. Legacy alongside Python, but plenty of office automation still runs on it.

commands.name: Ellipse
commands.description: Draws an ellipse from a centre and two axis lengths, or by bounding corners. Used for elliptical plans, arches and lighting layouts.

commands.name: Ellipsoid
commands.description: Creates a solid ellipsoid stretched along three axes. Useful for blob-like massing and organic volume placeholders.

commands.name: EMap
commands.description: Reflects a chosen environment image in the model's surfaces as a quality check. Simulates how a polished or glazed finish will reveal surface defects.

commands.name: EMapOff
commands.description: Turns off the environment-map (chrome-ball style) analysis display and returns objects to normal shading. The off-switch after checking surface fairness with EMap reflections.

commands.name: EnableClippingPlane
commands.description: Re-activates clipping planes in chosen viewports so they cut the model again. Pairs with DisableClippingPlane for flicking section cuts on and off while you work.

commands.name: EndBulge
commands.description: Adjusts how strongly a curve or surface end holds its shape near a matched edge without breaking continuity. A fine-tuning tool used after Match or MatchSrf.

commands.name: Enter
commands.description: Acts exactly like pressing the Enter key. Exists so toolbar buttons and macros can confirm defaults or repeat the previous command without keyboard input.

commands.name: EnterEnd
commands.description: Sends Enter repeatedly until the current command has completely finished, however many nested prompts remain. A macro-writer's tool for guaranteeing a clean state before the next instruction.

commands.name: Environments
commands.description: Opens the Environments panel where rendering environments — HDRI backdrops, skylight sources, reflection settings — are created and assigned. Central to getting believable lighting in rendered views.

commands.name: EvaluatePt
commands.description: Reports the exact world or CPlane coordinates of a picked point. Everyday check for setting-out values and datum levels.

commands.name: EvaluateUVPt
commands.description: Reports the U and V parameter values at a picked location on a surface. A niche but occasionally vital utility when scripting, texture-mapping or diagnosing surface parameterisation.

commands.name: Exit
commands.description: Closes Rhino, prompting to save any unsaved changes first. The command-line equivalent of quitting from the File menu.

commands.name: Explode
commands.description: Breaks joined objects into their component curves, surfaces or mesh parts, and dissolves blocks and groups of segments. First step whenever a compound object needs part-by-part editing.

commands.name: ExplodeBlock
commands.description: Replaces block instances with copies of their component geometry, including bursting nested blocks in one go. Use it deliberately — you gain editability but lose the block link that kept instances coordinated.

commands.name: Export
commands.description: Writes the selected objects out to another file and format. Used constantly to issue geometry to consultants, fabricators and other software.

commands.name: ExportBitmaps
commands.description: Saves the bitmap textures embedded in the current file out to a folder on disk. Essential when a model arrives with packed textures and you need the images for editing or for another application.

commands.name: ExportBlockAttributes
commands.description: Writes the attribute data carried by block instances out to a spreadsheet-friendly file. This is how door schedules, fixture counts and similar tabulations get from a block-based model into Excel.

commands.name: ExportRuiFile
commands.description: Saves toolbar and interface customisations to an RUI file that can be backed up or shared. How an office distributes its standard toolbar setup across workstations.

commands.name: ExportWithOrigin
commands.description: Exports selected objects with a picked base point that becomes the new file's origin. Vital for keeping shared coordinates sane when exchanging fragments of large site models.

commands.name: Extend
commands.description: Lengthens a curve to meet a boundary or by a set distance, keeping its character by line, arc or smooth continuation. Constantly used to make curves reach trimming edges.

commands.name: ExtendCrvOnSrf
commands.description: Extends a curve that lies on a surface along its natural path until it reaches the surface edges. Perfect for completing trim curves and panel lines that stop short of the boundary.

commands.name: ExtendDynamic
commands.description: Extends a curve by dragging its endpoint to wherever you want it, with the extension following the curve smoothly. The freehand cousin of Extend for when you don't have a boundary to extend to.

commands.name: ExtendSrf
commands.description: Lengthens a surface beyond a chosen edge, smoothly or as a straight continuation. Handy when a roof or wall surface falls just short of the geometry it must trim against.

commands.name: ExtractAnalysisMesh
commands.description: Pulls out the fine mesh Rhino built for a visual analysis (curvature, draft angle, zebra) as a real mesh object you can keep. Useful when you want that high-quality mesh for export or further processing.

commands.name: ExtractBadSrf
commands.description: Pulls the invalid faces out of polysurfaces so they can be repaired or rebuilt in isolation. Surgical follow-up to SelBadObjects on complex models.

commands.name: ExtractConnectedMeshFaces
commands.description: Selects and extracts all mesh faces connected to a picked face, optionally stopping at edges sharper than a given angle. Great for splitting a scan into logical regions — a roof plane, a wall face — along its natural creases.

commands.name: ExtractControlPolygon
commands.description: Creates a polyline (for curves) or mesh (for surfaces) that duplicates the control polygon — the straight-line cage joining the control points. Useful for analysing structure or reusing the cage as construction geometry.

commands.name: ExtractCurvatureGraph
commands.description: Converts the on-screen curvature-graph display into actual curve objects. Lets you keep, print or dimension the curvature 'porcupine' as documentary evidence of a curve's fairness.

commands.name: ExtractDuplicateMeshFaces
commands.description: Finds faces that exist twice in a mesh — a common flaw in imported and merged meshes — and pulls the duplicates out as a separate mesh for inspection or deletion. Duplicate faces break 3D printing and boolean operations, so this is a standard repair pass.

commands.name: ExtractIsocurve
commands.description: Pulls a chosen U or V isocurve off a surface as a real curve. Used to harvest clean construction curves that follow a surface's natural flow.

commands.name: ExtractMeshFaces
commands.description: Detaches selected faces from a mesh into a separate mesh object. Used to isolate a roof plane or facade zone from a context scan.

commands.name: ExtractMeshFacesByArea
commands.description: Separates mesh faces whose area falls within a range you specify into their own mesh. A diagnostic and repair filter for isolating suspiciously tiny (or huge) faces in scan data.

commands.name: ExtractMeshFacesByAspectRatio
commands.description: Separates mesh faces whose aspect ratio exceeds a threshold — the long thin slivers — into their own mesh. Isolate them, inspect them, then repair or delete without touching the healthy faces.

commands.name: ExtractMeshFacesByDraftAngle
commands.description: Separates mesh faces whose slope relative to a pull direction falls within a chosen range. Useful far beyond moulding: pull all roof planes from a terrain scan, or every overhanging face from a print check.

commands.name: ExtractMeshFacesByEdgeLength
commands.description: Separates mesh faces containing edges shorter or longer than limits you set into their own mesh. Another of the criteria filters for hunting down problem geometry inside big meshes.

commands.name: ExtractMeshPart
commands.description: Pulls out one connected region of a disjoint mesh as its own object. Quick way to separate buildings merged into a single downloaded city mesh.

commands.name: ExtractNonManifoldMeshEdges
commands.description: Finds edges shared by more than two faces — non-manifold junctions that make a mesh unprintable and unbooleanable — and extracts the offending faces for repair. A core step in preparing meshes for 3D printing.

commands.name: ExtractPt
commands.description: Creates point objects at the control points, edit points or vertices of the selected geometry. Useful for rebuilding geometry from its defining points, or exporting point sets to other software.

commands.name: ExtractRenderMesh
commands.description: Copies the display mesh Rhino generated for a surface or solid out as an editable mesh object. The standard way to get a mesh that matches exactly what you see shaded on screen — often as a starting point for export or mesh editing.

commands.name: ExtractSrf
commands.description: Separates chosen faces from a polysurface so they become independent surfaces, leaving the rest behind. Used to isolate a facade panel or roof face for detailed work.

commands.name: ExtractSubCrv
commands.description: Copies (or removes) the portion of a curve between two picked points as a separate curve. Cleaner than split-and-delete when you need just one segment of a longer curve.

commands.name: ExtractUVMesh
commands.description: Creates a flat mesh laid out in a surface's UV parameter space. Paired with ApplyMesh or ApplyMeshUVN, it forms a round-trip workflow: flatten, design in 2D, wrap the result back onto the 3D surface.

commands.name: ExtractWireframe
commands.description: Converts the displayed isocurve wireframe of surfaces or polysurfaces into curves in one go. Quick source of a full curve network for diagrams and pattern studies.

commands.name: ExtrudeCrv
commands.description: Pushes a curve in a straight direction to form a surface, or a closed solid with caps. The workhorse for turning plans into walls and profiles into massing.

commands.name: ExtrudeCrvAlongCrv
commands.description: Extrudes a profile curve along the length of another curve, keeping the profile orientation fixed. Useful for angled glazing bars and raked structural members where a sweep would rotate the section.

commands.name: ExtrudeCrvTapered
commands.description: Extrudes a curve with a draft angle so the sides lean in or out as they rise. Used for battered walls, formwork with draft and tapered massing studies.

commands.name: ExtrudeCrvToPoint
commands.description: Extrudes a curve so it tapers to a single apex point. Instant tool for pyramidal roofs, spires and cone-like transitions from any plan shape.

commands.name: ExtrudeMesh
commands.description: Extrudes mesh faces or whole meshes in a straight line, creating new connected mesh volume. The mesh-world equivalent of extruding surfaces — often used to give thickness to open scan patches.

commands.name: ExtrudeSrf
commands.description: Thickens a surface by extruding it straight into a closed solid. Used to give floor plates and panels physical depth for booleans and sections.

commands.name: ExtrudeSrfAlongCrv
commands.description: Sweeps a surface along a path curve, producing the solid it traces out. Useful for creating swept solids where a profile face must travel a curved route — a moulded string, a curved wall from its section.

commands.name: ExtrudeSrfTapered
commands.description: Extrudes a surface with a draft angle so its sides slope as they rise. Useful for foundations, moulds and casting geometry needing release angles.

commands.name: ExtrudeSrfToPoint
commands.description: Extrudes a surface so it tapers to a single apex point, producing a pyramid- or cone-like solid from any face. Handy for spires, funnels and quick massing of pitched forms.

commands.name: ExtrudeSubD
commands.description: Extrudes SubD faces or edges outwards, adding connected new faces while keeping everything a single smooth SubD. One of the fundamental moves of SubD box-modelling — grow limbs, fins and volumes straight out of the form.

commands.name: Fair
commands.description: Gently re-smooths a curve to remove kinks and wobbles in its curvature while keeping close to its original shape. Used on imported or traced curves before building quality surfaces from them.

commands.name: Fillet
commands.description: Joins two curves with a tangent arc of a given radius, trimming them back to meet it. The standard way to round corners in plans and profiles.

commands.name: FilletCorners
commands.description: Rounds every corner of a polyline or polycurve with one radius in a single operation. Saves picking corner pairs one by one on panel outlines and plan shapes.

commands.name: FilletEdge
commands.description: Rounds selected edges of a solid with constant or variable radii, handling the corner patches automatically. The standard finishing tool for softening built edges before rendering or fabrication.

commands.name: FilletSrf
commands.description: Inserts a constant-radius rounded surface between two surfaces and can trim them to fit. Used for radiused junctions between individual surfaces rather than solid edges.

commands.name: FillMeshHole
commands.description: Caps a single naked hole in a mesh with new faces. Quick patching during mesh repair for printing or rendering.

commands.name: FillMeshHoles
commands.description: Caps every closed naked border in a mesh in one pass. The bulk version of FillMeshHole for making scans watertight.

commands.name: Fin
commands.description: Extrudes a curve lying on a surface along the surface's normals (or at an angle to them), creating a fin-like surface that stands off the base. Ideal for ribs, brims, flanges and stiffeners that must follow a curved parent surface.

commands.name: FindText
commands.description: Searches the model for text objects, dots, leaders and annotations containing a given string, and can zoom to and select the matches. Lifesaver on large drawing files when you need to find every instance of a room name or note.

commands.name: FitCrv
commands.description: Refits a curve to a given tolerance with fewer control points. A quick way to tame dense curves from tracing, intersections or imported data.

commands.name: FitSrf
commands.description: Refits a surface to a specified tolerance, adjusting its control-point structure — often dramatically simplifying over-dense surfaces. Use it to lighten heavy imported surfaces while keeping shape deviation within tolerance.

commands.name: FixedLengthCrvEdit
commands.description: Lets you drag and reshape a curve while Rhino preserves its overall length exactly. Invaluable when the curve represents something physically inextensible — a cable, chain, strip of material — that must keep its length as it moves.

commands.name: FlatShade
commands.description: Toggles flat shading in the viewport, rendering each mesh facet as a hard plane instead of smoothing across them. Reveals the true underlying render mesh — useful for judging mesh density and diagnosing shading artefacts.

commands.name: FlattenSrf
commands.description: Produces a flat, planar version of a surface based on its untrimmed UV structure, keeping the trim curves in place on the flat copy. Combined with ApplyCrv and ApplyMesh, it underpins flatten–design–rewrap workflows for decorating curved surfaces.

commands.name: Flip
commands.description: Reverses the direction of curves, or the normals of surfaces and meshes. Fixes offsets going the wrong way and dark, inside-out faces in renders.

commands.name: Flow
commands.description: Re-shapes objects from along a straight base curve onto a target curve, bending them to follow it. The classic trick for modelling straight, then curving the result along a path.

commands.name: FlowAlongSrf
commands.description: Maps objects from a flat base surface onto a target surface, morphing them to its curvature. The standard route for applying panel systems and patterns designed flat onto doubly curved facades.

commands.name: Fullscreen
commands.description: Expands the viewport to fill the screen, hiding interface panels. Ideal for design reviews and client presentations without leaving Rhino.

commands.name: GCon
commands.description: Reports the geometric continuity — G0 position, G1 tangency, G2 curvature — between the ends of two curves. The objective test when you need to know whether two curves genuinely flow into one another.

commands.name: GetDocumentUserText
commands.description: Reads and reports the document user text stored in the file — the named key/value pairs such as project number or revision. Chiefly useful in scripts and macros that need those values.

commands.name: GetUserText
commands.description: Reads and reports the user text attached to selected objects — per-object key/value data such as part numbers or specifications. The retrieval half of Rhino's simple object-data system, alongside SetUserText.

commands.name: GlobalEdgeContinuity
commands.description: Displays continuity analysis across the matched edges of a model at once, rather than one edge pair at a time. Lets surface modellers audit an entire patch layout for position, tangency and curvature quality in a single view.

commands.name: GradientView
commands.description: Toggles a graduated background in the viewport in place of the flat background colour. Purely cosmetic, but a two-tone backdrop instantly makes screenshots and client-facing views feel more finished.

commands.name: Grasshopper
commands.description: Opens Grasshopper, Rhino's visual programming environment for parametric and generative design. The centre of computational workflows from facade panelisation to environmental studies.

commands.name: GrasshopperDeveloperSettings
commands.description: Opens Grasshopper's developer settings, controlling assembly folders and how add-on libraries are loaded. Strictly for people writing or debugging Grasshopper components.

commands.name: GrasshopperFolders
commands.description: Opens Grasshopper's special folders — Libraries, UserObjects and friends — directly in the file explorer. The quick route to installing a downloaded plug-in or backing up custom clusters.

commands.name: GrasshopperGetSDKDocumentation
commands.description: Retrieves the Grasshopper SDK documentation for component developers. Only relevant if you are programming your own Grasshopper components.

commands.name: GrasshopperLoadOneByOne
commands.description: Loads Grasshopper add-on libraries one at a time with a prompt between each, so a crashing or misbehaving plug-in can be identified by elimination. The classic troubleshooting mode when Grasshopper will not start cleanly.

commands.name: GrasshopperPlayer
commands.description: Runs a Grasshopper definition as if it were a native command, prompting for inputs without opening the canvas. Lets teams share parametric tools with colleagues who never touch Grasshopper.

commands.name: GrasshopperPluginList
commands.description: Reports the Grasshopper add-on libraries present in this installation. Useful for auditing what is loaded when diagnosing conflicts or documenting a workstation setup.

commands.name: Grid
commands.description: Adjusts the construction plane grid's extents, spacing and snap intervals. Worth setting early so the grid matches your project's planning module.

commands.name: GroundPlane
commands.description: Controls the infinite ground plane used in rendered and raytraced views — its height, material and whether it only catches shadows. The fastest way to ground a model so renders stop floating in space.

commands.name: Group
commands.description: Binds selected objects into a group that selects as one. Light-touch organisation for furniture sets and repeated assemblies that do not warrant a block.

commands.name: Gumball
commands.description: Toggles the on-object widget that drags, rotates and scales selections along its arrows and arcs, with extrude and copy modifiers. Most designers leave it on as their primary hands-on transform tool.

commands.name: GumballAlignment
commands.description: Sets which frame the gumball widget aligns to — the construction plane, the object itself, or world axes. Switching alignment is the difference between dragging a rotated panel along its own edge and along the world grid.

commands.name: GumballAutoReset
commands.description: Toggles whether a manually relocated gumball snaps back to its default position after each use, or stays where you put it. A workflow preference for heavy gumball users who repeatedly transform about a custom pivot.

commands.name: GumballRelocate
commands.description: Moves and reorients the gumball widget itself without moving the selected objects, setting a custom pivot and axes for the next transformation. Essential for rotating or scaling about a specific corner, edge or datum rather than the selection's centre.

commands.name: GumballReset
commands.description: Returns the gumball widget to its default position, orientation and settings for the current selection. The quick fix after relocating or reorienting the gumball leaves it somewhere unhelpful.

commands.name: GumballScaleMode
commands.description: Sets how the gumball's scale handles behave — whether dragging one handle scales in that single direction or scales the selection uniformly in all directions. Worth knowing so a quick handle-drag stretches or resizes exactly as intended.

commands.name: GumballSettings
commands.description: Opens the settings for the gumball manipulation widget, letting you tune drag behaviour, snapping and which handles are shown. Reach for it when the gumball feels too twitchy or is cluttering the viewport.

commands.name: HandleCurve
commands.description: Draws a curve by placing points with adjustable tangent handles, much like pen-tool drawing in illustration software. Useful when you want direct control over tangency as you sketch a profile.

commands.name: Hatch
commands.description: Fills closed boundaries with a pattern or solid fill. Brings plans and sections up to drawing standard with material and poche indication.

commands.name: HatchBase
commands.description: Sets the base point from which hatch patterns are measured, so pattern lines align consistently across a drawing. Designers use it to line up brick or tile hatches with actual wall setting-out.

commands.name: HatchScale
commands.description: Controls the global scaling applied to hatch patterns in the model, so you can tune pattern density across every hatch at once. Handy when hatches read too dense or too sparse at your printing scale.

commands.name: HBar
commands.description: Turns on the handlebar editor, which lets you drag a tangent handlebar along a curve or surface to reshape it intuitively. A friendlier alternative to raw control-point editing for smooth shape tweaks.

commands.name: Heightfield
commands.description: Generates a relief surface or mesh from the light and dark values of an image. Handy for quick terrain from greyscale maps and textured feature walls.

commands.name: Helix
commands.description: Draws a 3D helix around an axis with a set number of turns and pitch. The base curve for spiral stairs, coiled details and threaded forms.

commands.name: Help
commands.description: Opens Rhino's help system, jumping to the topic for the current command when one is running. The quickest way to check a command's options mid-task.

commands.name: Hide
commands.description: Makes selected objects invisible without deleting them. Constant tool for decluttering the view while working on something behind or inside.

commands.name: HideInDetail
commands.description: Hides the selected objects only within the active layout detail, leaving them visible in the model and in other details. Essential for tailoring what each drawing view shows on a sheet.

commands.name: HideLayersInDetail
commands.description: Turns off the layers of the selected objects, but only in the active layout detail. Lets each detail on a sheet show a different mix of layers without touching the model-wide layer states.

commands.name: HidePt
commands.description: Hides the selected control points so they stay out of the way while you edit the rest. Useful on dense point grids where accidental grabs are a constant risk.

commands.name: HideSwap
commands.description: Swaps the visibility state of everything: hidden objects become visible and visible objects become hidden. A quick way to flip between two working sets of geometry.

commands.name: HighlightObjectLayers
commands.description: Highlights the layers of the selected objects in the Layers panel so you can see instantly where things live. A lifesaver in models with long, deeply nested layer trees.

commands.name: History
commands.description: Controls recording of parent-child links so edits to input curves update dependent surfaces automatically. Powerful for iterative design where profiles keep changing after lofts and sweeps are built.

commands.name: HistoryPurge
commands.description: Removes construction-history records from the selected objects, breaking the parent-child update link. Do this when history is no longer wanted or is causing unexpected updates.

commands.name: HistoryUpdate
commands.description: Forces history-linked child objects to update to match their edited parents. Used when history updating is set to manual, or when you want to trigger a refresh on demand.

commands.name: Hydrostatics
commands.description: Calculates hydrostatic values such as displaced volume, waterline area and centre of buoyancy for hull-like surfaces and solids. A marine design tool for checking how a hull sits in the water.

commands.name: Hyperbola
commands.description: Draws a hyperbola from focus and vertex parameters. A niche precision curve for shell structures and reflector studies.

commands.name: Hyperlink
commands.description: Attaches a web address to an object so supporting information, such as a product page or specification, is one click away. Useful for embedding references directly into a model.

commands.name: IgesImportOptions
commands.description: Sets the options Rhino uses when importing IGES files, such as which translation preset to apply. Reach for it when IGES data from a consultant comes in badly and needs different import handling.

commands.name: Import
commands.description: Brings geometry from another file into the current model, converting from formats like DWG, IGES, STEP, SKP and OBJ. The daily bridge to consultant and product data.

commands.name: ImportAnnotationStyles
