commands.description: Imports annotation styles from another Rhino file into the current model, so dimensions and text match office standards. Saves rebuilding styles by hand on every new project.

commands.name: ImportLayout
commands.description: Brings layout pages from another Rhino file into the current model, including their details and title-block geometry. Ideal for reusing a practice's standard sheet setups.

commands.name: IncrementalSave
commands.description: Saves a numbered copy each time it runs, building a version trail. A lightweight manual version control habit for design development.

commands.name: InfinitePlane
commands.description: Creates an infinite plane object that other commands can use, for example as a cutter in intersections or booleans where a bounded plane would be too small. A construction helper rather than final geometry.

commands.name: Insert
commands.description: Places an instance of a block definition, or an external file as a block, at a chosen point and scale. The entry point for component-based and referenced modelling.

commands.name: InsertControlPoint
commands.description: Adds a control point to a curve, or a whole row of points to a surface, where you click. Gives finer local control before detailed point editing.

commands.name: InsertEdge
commands.description: Adds new edge loops across SubD faces to tighten or add detail in a region. The main way to control how crisp or soft a sculpted feature reads.

commands.name: InsertEditPoint
commands.description: Adds an edit point to a curve, inserting the underlying knot so the curve gains a new point it passes through. Useful when you edit curves via edit points rather than control points.

commands.name: InsertKink
commands.description: Inserts a kink at a chosen point on a curve so it can form a sharp corner there. Use it when a smooth curve needs to break into an angle without being split into pieces.

commands.name: InsertKnot
commands.description: Adds a knot to a curve or surface, creating extra control points at that parameter without changing the shape. Gives finer local editing control exactly where you need it.

commands.name: InsertLineIntoCrv
commands.description: Replaces the portion of a curve between two picked points with a straight line segment. A tidy way to flatten part of a freeform curve without trimming and rejoining by hand.

commands.name: InsertPoint
commands.description: Adds vertices along SubD edges, splitting the neighbouring faces. Fine-grained alternative to InsertEdge when only part of a loop needs extra control.

commands.name: Inset
commands.description: Creates a smaller face inside a chosen face at a set margin, ready to push or pull. Added in Rhino 8, it pairs with PushPull for panelled and recessed detailing.

commands.name: InterpCrv
commands.description: Draws a smooth curve that passes exactly through each picked point. Reach for it when tracing site outlines, sections or scanned drawings where the curve must hit known positions.

commands.name: InterpCrvOnSrf
commands.description: Draws an interpolated curve that lies directly on a surface, following its curvature between picked points. Useful for laying out seams, panel joints or path lines across doubly curved forms.

commands.name: Intersect
commands.description: Creates curves or points where selected objects cross each other. Used constantly to find true junction lines between roofs, walls and complex surfaces.

commands.name: IntersectSelf
commands.description: Finds the places where an object crosses itself and marks the self-intersections. Helpful for diagnosing problem curves or meshes before offsets, booleans or fabrication.

commands.name: IntersectTwoSets
commands.description: Intersects every object in one set with the objects in a second set, ignoring intersections within each set. Cleaner than plain Intersect when you only care about crossings between two families of geometry.

commands.name: Invert
commands.description: Swaps the selection to everything currently unselected. Handy trick: select what you want to keep, invert, then hide or delete the rest.

commands.name: InvertPt
commands.description: Inverts the current control-point selection, deselecting picked points and selecting the rest. Speeds up point editing when it is easier to pick what you do not want.

commands.name: Isolate
commands.description: Hides everything except the selected objects in one step. The fastest way to focus on a single element inside a dense model.

commands.name: IsolateLock
commands.description: Isolates the selection by locking everything else instead of hiding it, so surrounding geometry stays visible for context but cannot be selected or snagged. Good for focused edits inside a busy model.

commands.name: IsolateToViewports
commands.description: Isolates the selected objects on a per-viewport basis, hiding everything else only in the chosen viewport while other viewports stay complete. Useful for comparing a focused view with the full model side by side.

commands.name: Isometric
commands.description: Sets the viewport to an isometric parallel projection from a chosen quadrant such as north-east or south-west. The classic axonometric-style view architects use for explanatory drawings.

commands.name: Join
commands.description: Connects touching curves into polycurves, or surfaces into polysurfaces and closed solids. The glue command used constantly to assemble edited geometry back together.

commands.name: JoinEdge
commands.description: Force-joins two naked edges that sit outside joining tolerance. A repair tool of last resort for gappy polysurfaces; use sparingly as it hides rather than fixes the underlying gap.

commands.name: Lasso
commands.description: Selects objects by drawing a freehand loop around them, rather than a rectangular window. Handy when the things you want are scattered among things you do not.

commands.name: Layer
commands.description: Opens the layers panel to create, rename, colour and structure layers and sublayers. The heart of model organisation in every professional Rhino file.

commands.name: Layer States
commands.description: Opens the Layer States panel, where you save and restore snapshots of layer visibility, colour and lock settings. Perfect for flipping between drawing setups such as plans, presentations and working states.

commands.name: LayerBook
commands.description: Steps through the model's layers one at a time like slides, showing each in turn. Useful for assembly sequences or walking a client through a scheme layer by layer.

commands.name: LayerStateManager
commands.description: Saves and restores named combinations of layer visibility, colour and locking. Lets one model serve many outputs, like planning drawings versus detail packages.

commands.name: Layout
commands.description: Creates a paper-space page with a title-block-ready sheet and viewports onto the model. The starting point for issuing scaled, printable drawings straight from Rhino.

commands.name: LayoutProperties
commands.description: Edits the properties of the active layout page, such as its name and paper size. Use it to fix a sheet set up at the wrong size without recreating it.

commands.name: Layouts
commands.description: Opens the Layouts panel listing every layout page in the file for quick navigation, renaming and management. Much faster than tab-hunting in documents with many sheets.

commands.name: Leader
commands.description: Draws an arrowed leader line with attached text. The standard tool for calling up notes against specific parts of a drawing.

commands.name: Length
commands.description: Reports the true length of curves and edges. Used for quantities such as handrail runs, skirting lengths and cable routes.

commands.name: Libraries
commands.description: Opens the Libraries panel for browsing content such as materials, environments and textures, ready to drag into the model. A shop window for render assets.

commands.name: Lights
commands.description: Opens the Lights panel listing all lights in the model, where you can select, toggle and edit them. The control room for a rendering's lighting setup.

commands.name: Line
commands.description: Draws a single straight line between two picked points. The most basic drafting tool, used constantly for construction lines, edges and setting-out geometry.

commands.name: Lines
commands.description: Draws a connected chain of line segments where each segment becomes a separate line object, unlike Polyline which makes one joined object. Useful when you want individually editable segments.

commands.name: LineThroughPt
commands.description: Fits a single best-fit line through a set of selected points. A quick regression helper for finding the underlying direction in survey points or scan data.

commands.name: LinetypeDisplay
commands.description: Controls how linetypes such as dashed and dotted patterns display in model viewports, including their scaling. Lets you check that centre lines and hidden lines will read correctly before printing.

commands.name: Linetypes
commands.description: Opens the document's linetype list, where you load and manage dash patterns used by curves and layers. Set these up early so drawings export and print with correct line conventions.

commands.name: List
commands.description: Dumps the full internal data structure of an object, down to knots and control points. A deep debugging tool for advanced users and developers.

commands.name: LoadScript
commands.description: Loads a RhinoScript file into the session so its subroutines are available to run. Part of the classic RhinoScript automation workflow.

commands.name: Lock
commands.description: Makes selected objects visible but unselectable, greyed in the viewport. Perfect for reference geometry and context you must see but never nudge.

commands.name: LockSwap
commands.description: Swaps the locked state of everything: locked objects unlock and unlocked objects lock. Quick for alternating between editing a set of objects and protecting it.

commands.name: LockViewport
commands.description: Locks the active detail so its view cannot be accidentally panned or zoomed. Essential once a layout detail is set to a precise drawing scale.

commands.name: Loft
commands.description: Fits a surface through an ordered series of profile curves, with style options from tight to loose. A staple for canopies, hulls and any form defined by cross-sections.

commands.name: Login
commands.description: Signs in to your Rhino account for licensing and cloud services. Needed when using Cloud Zoo licences or shared team resources.

commands.name: Logout
commands.description: Signs out of your Rhino account, releasing the licence and cloud services on this machine. Use it before switching accounts or freeing a licence for a colleague.

commands.name: MacroEditor
commands.description: Opens an editor for writing and testing command macros, with a button to run them directly. The stepping stone between typed commands and full scripting.

commands.name: Macros
commands.description: Opens the Macros panel where command macros can be stored, organised and run without writing full scripts. A convenient home for the repetitive command sequences you use every day.

commands.name: Maelstrom
commands.description: Spirals objects around an axis so they whirl progressively with radius. A specialist deformer for vortex-like patterns and twisted radial compositions.

commands.name: Make2D
commands.description: Generates flat 2D line drawings of the model from a view, with hidden lines on separate layers. The bridge from 3D model to plans, sections and elevations for drafting.

commands.name: MakeHole
commands.description: Cuts a hole through a solid using a closed profile curve you supply. The general-purpose opening cutter for shaped penetrations and window reveals.

commands.name: MakeNonPeriodic
commands.description: Converts a closed periodic curve or surface into a non-periodic one, introducing a seam that can hold a kink. Sometimes needed before edits that require a defined start and end.

commands.name: MakePeriodic
commands.description: Converts a closed curve or surface so it has no kink at its seam, making it smoothly continuous all the way round. Useful before building smooth closed lofts or revolves.

commands.name: MakeSubDFriendly
commands.description: Rebuilds a curve so its structure suits SubD tools, avoiding surprises when creating SubD geometry from curves. Run it on profile curves before lofting or sweeping into SubD.

commands.name: MakeUniform
commands.description: Makes the knot spacing of a curve or surface uniform, evening out how control points influence the shape. The geometry may shift slightly, so use it on design surfaces rather than fitted data.

commands.name: MakeUniformUV
commands.description: Makes a surface's knot spacing uniform in the U or V direction you choose, rather than both at once. Gives more control than MakeUniform when only one direction is misbehaving.

commands.name: MappingWidget
commands.description: Shows the texture-mapping widget for the selected objects so you can move, rotate and scale how textures wrap onto them. Reach for it when a material's pattern sits at the wrong size or angle.

commands.name: MappingWidgetOff
commands.description: Hides the texture-mapping widgets shown by MappingWidget. Tidies the viewport once mapping adjustments are done.

commands.name: MarkFoci
commands.description: Places point objects at the foci of selected ellipses and conic curves. Useful for setting-out geometry that depends on focal points, such as reflector or whispering-gallery studies.

commands.name: Match
commands.description: Adjusts the end of one curve to meet another with position, tangency or curvature continuity. Essential prep before lofting or sweeping surfaces that must flow together.

commands.name: MatchAnnotation
commands.description: Applies the properties of one annotation to other annotations so notes and dimensions read consistently. A quick fix for drawings where text and dimension formatting has drifted.

commands.name: MatchCrvDir
commands.description: Flips the direction of curves to match a master curve. Worth running before lofting or sweeping, where mismatched curve directions cause twisted results.

commands.name: MatchLayer
commands.description: Moves selected objects onto the layer of a picked target object. Faster than hunting through the Layers panel when tidying a model's organisation.

commands.name: MatchMapping
commands.description: Copies texture mapping from a source object onto other objects so a material's pattern flows consistently across them. Saves redoing mapping widgets object by object.

commands.name: MatchMeshEdge
commands.description: Moves mesh vertices so neighbouring naked edges line up and close small gaps. Used when separate mesh parts almost meet but leave hairline cracks.

commands.name: MatchProperties
commands.description: Copies display and object properties such as layer, colour and linetype from one object to others. Fast way to bring rogue imports in line with your drawing standards.

commands.name: MatchSrf
commands.description: Adjusts a surface edge to meet a neighbouring surface with position, tangency or curvature continuity. The key tool for achieving seamless multi-patch surfaces in high-quality modelling.

commands.name: Materials
commands.description: Opens the Materials panel where render materials are created, edited and assigned. The main workspace for defining how surfaces look in renderings.

commands.name: Maximize
commands.description: Maximises the Rhino application window to fill the screen. A window-management convenience mainly used from scripts and macros.

commands.name: MaxViewport
commands.description: Toggles the active viewport between maximised and the multi-view layout. Usually driven by double-clicking the viewport title.

commands.name: Merge2MeshFaces
commands.description: Merges two adjacent mesh faces into a single face. A small-scale clean-up tool for simplifying unnecessarily triangulated areas of a mesh.

commands.name: MergeAllCoplanarFaces
commands.description: Dissolves unnecessary edges between flat faces that lie in the same plane. Tidies solids after booleans so they read cleanly and export with fewer faces.

commands.name: MergeAllEdges
commands.description: Merges adjacent edge segments along surface and polysurface borders into single edges wherever they meet smoothly. Tidies fragmented edge counts left behind by trims and joins.

commands.name: MergeCoplanarFace
commands.description: Merges a picked planar face of a polysurface with its adjacent coplanar faces, simplifying boxy solids after booleans. Reduces face clutter without changing the shape.

commands.name: MergeEdge
commands.description: Merges adjacent edge segments of a surface or polysurface into one edge. Use it on a specific edge chain when MergeAllEdges is more than you need.

commands.name: MergeFaces
commands.description: Combines adjacent SubD or mesh faces into a single larger face. Used to simplify topology after heavy editing.

commands.name: MergeSrf
commands.description: Combines two untrimmed surfaces sharing an edge into one single surface. Useful for simplifying models before offsetting, unrolling or exporting.

commands.name: Mesh
commands.description: Converts NURBS surfaces, polysurfaces or SubD into a polygon mesh with density controls. Used before 3D printing, export to game engines or heavy visualisation scenes.

commands.name: MeshBooleanDifference
commands.description: Subtracts one set of closed meshes from another. Used to cut openings in scan or export meshes without converting to NURBS.

commands.name: MeshBooleanIntersection
commands.description: Keeps only the shared volume of intersecting closed meshes. Handy for clash volumes and trimming context meshes to a site boundary.

commands.name: MeshBooleanSplit
commands.description: Splits meshes into parts along their mutual intersections, keeping all pieces. Useful for dividing terrain meshes along plot boundaries.

commands.name: MeshBooleanUnion
commands.description: Merges overlapping closed meshes into a single mesh. The mesh counterpart to BooleanUnion for print-ready models.

commands.name: MeshBox
commands.description: Creates a box directly as a mesh with set face counts. Useful for lightweight massing in mesh-based workflows and export pipelines.

commands.name: MeshCone
commands.description: Creates a cone as a polygon mesh. A quick faceted primitive for context and export models.

commands.name: MeshCylinder
commands.description: Creates a cylinder as a polygon mesh. Used where lightweight faceted geometry is preferable to NURBS, such as context models.

commands.name: MeshEllipsoid
commands.description: Creates an ellipsoid as a mesh primitive rather than a NURBS surface. Handy when building lightweight massing or export-ready mesh scenes.

commands.name: MeshFromLines
commands.description: Builds a mesh whose edges follow a network of intersecting lines. Useful for turning a drawn wireframe grid, such as a space-frame layout, directly into mesh faces.

commands.name: MeshFromPoints
commands.description: Creates mesh faces over an ordered grid of points. Useful for reconstructing terrain or scanned grids as a single mesh surface.

commands.name: MeshIntersect
commands.description: Intersects meshes with each other and returns the intersection as polylines. The mesh counterpart of Intersect, useful for section lines through scanned or exported models.

commands.name: MeshOutline
commands.description: Draws the outline of a mesh as seen from the current view as a planar curve. Great for site plan silhouettes of context models and quick shadow footprints.

commands.name: MeshPatch
commands.description: Fills a set of curves and points with a triangulated mesh patch. A quick route from surveyed contours or scattered spot levels to a terrain mesh.

commands.name: MeshPlane
commands.description: Creates a rectangular mesh plane with a set grid of faces. A common base for terrain sculpting and drape-style studies in mesh workflows.

commands.name: MeshPolyline
commands.description: Fills a closed polyline with mesh faces, turning an outline directly into a flat mesh. Useful for quick planar mesh panels without going through NURBS surfaces.

commands.name: MeshRepair
commands.description: Opens a guided panel that checks a mesh and walks through fixing its defects step by step. The first stop when a downloaded or scanned mesh refuses to print or boolean.

commands.name: MeshSelfIntersect
commands.description: Finds the places where a mesh passes through itself and marks them. An important check before 3D printing or exporting, where self-intersections cause failures.

commands.name: MeshSphere
commands.description: Creates a sphere as a polygon mesh with controllable density. Handy for placeholder objects in scenes destined for real-time or print output.

commands.name: MeshSplit
commands.description: Splits a mesh with curves, surfaces or other meshes without needing closed volumes. The general-purpose divider for open meshes like terrain.

commands.name: MeshToNURB
commands.description: Converts every mesh face into a NURBS surface joined as a polysurface. A blunt but effective route when downstream tools demand NURBS, best kept for small meshes.

commands.name: MeshTorus
commands.description: Creates a ring as a polygon mesh. Occasionally useful for faceted loops in visualisation scenes.

commands.name: MeshTrim
commands.description: Cuts away the picked side of a mesh along a curve or surface. Everyday tool for trimming site meshes to boundaries.

commands.name: MeshTruncatedCone
commands.description: Creates a truncated cone as a mesh primitive. One of the mesh equivalents of Rhino's solid primitives, for lightweight or export-focused modelling.

commands.name: MigratePlugins
commands.description: Brings plug-ins installed in a previous Rhino version across to the current one. Run it after upgrading so your toolset follows you.

commands.name: Minimize
commands.description: Minimises the Rhino application window to the taskbar. Mostly useful in scripts that hand control to another program temporarily.

commands.name: Mirror
commands.description: Reflects objects across a line or plane, optionally keeping the original. Essential for symmetrical plans, handed apartment types and reflected details.

commands.name: MirrorHole
commands.description: Mirrors an existing hole feature across a line on the same planar solid face. Quicker than cutting a matching hole from scratch on symmetrical parts.

commands.name: ModelBasepoint
commands.description: Sets the base point used when this file is inserted or linked into another model. Set it deliberately so blocks and references land where you expect, for example on a site datum.

commands.name: ModifyRadius
commands.description: Changes the radius of an existing circle or arc without redrawing it. A fast, precise edit for setting-out geometry.

commands.name: Move
commands.description: Moves objects from a base point to a target point with full snapping precision. The most fundamental transform, preferred over dragging when accuracy matters.

commands.name: MoveEdge
commands.description: Moves a single edge of a solid while the connected faces stretch to keep the body closed. Useful for tweaking wedge angles and ridge lines directly.

commands.name: MoveFace
commands.description: Pushes or pulls a face of a solid, extending the neighbouring faces to follow. Quick parametric-feeling edits like making a box taller or a recess deeper without remodelling.

commands.name: MoveHole
commands.description: Slides an existing hole to a new position within its planar face. Saves re-cutting openings when a penetration needs repositioning.

commands.name: MoveTargetToObjects
commands.description: Moves the view camera's target onto the selected objects so orbiting pivots around them. Cures the frustration of a view that rotates about empty space.

commands.name: MoveUntrimmedEdge
commands.description: Drags an untrimmed surface edge to a new position, reshaping the surface while keeping its structure. A direct-editing tool for simple surface adjustments.

commands.name: MoveUVN
commands.description: Nudges control points along a surface's U, V and normal directions with sliders and smoothing. A precise sculpting panel for refining surface interiors without breaking edges.

commands.name: MPlane
commands.description: Attaches a mobile construction plane to an object so the CPlane follows the object as it moves or rotates. Very useful when detailing components that sit at odd angles.

commands.name: MultiPause
commands.description: A macro helper that pauses a macro for any number of user picks until Enter is pressed. Use it where a plain Pause, which accepts one input, is not enough.

commands.name: MultiPipe
commands.description: Builds a smooth SubD pipe network over a set of connected curves, resolving the junctions automatically. Perfect for branching structures, node details and tubular furniture frames.

commands.name: Named CPlanes
commands.description: Opens the Named CPlanes panel, where construction planes can be saved and restored by name. Invaluable on projects with sloping or rotated setting-out grids.

commands.name: Named Positions
commands.description: Opens the Named Positions panel, which stores arrangements of objects so you can move things and later snap them back. Great for comparing design options or building exploded views.

commands.name: Named Views
commands.description: Opens the Named Views panel, where camera positions are saved and restored by name. The backbone of repeatable renders and consistent layout details.

commands.name: NamedCPlane
commands.description: Saves and restores construction planes by name. Keeps a library of working planes for each facade, roof pitch or datum in a project.

commands.name: NamedPosition
commands.description: Saves the current position of selected objects under a name so they can be returned there later, even after being moved. Useful for exploded axonometrics and option studies.

commands.name: NamedSelections
commands.description: Saves selection sets by name so a group of objects can be reselected in one click. A big time-saver for recurring edits on the same scattered set of geometry.

commands.name: NamedView
commands.description: Saves and restores camera positions by name, with thumbnails. Essential for repeatable render views and keeping agreed verified-view camera setups.

commands.name: NetworkSrf
commands.description: Builds a surface through a criss-crossing network of curves in two directions. Powerful for complex freeform patches where lofts and sweeps cannot capture the shape.

commands.name: New
commands.description: Starts a fresh model from a template that sets units and tolerances. Choosing the right template avoids tolerance headaches later.

commands.name: NewFloatingViewport
commands.description: Opens an extra viewport in its own window, ideal for a second monitor. Lets you keep a render view open while drafting in another.

commands.name: NewViewport
commands.description: Creates an additional viewport with its own camera and display settings. Useful for adding a dedicated perspective or detail view alongside the standard set.

commands.name: NextDetail
commands.description: Activates the next detail on the current layout. Lets you cycle through a sheet's views from the keyboard while setting them up.

commands.name: NextOrthoViewport
commands.description: Switches focus to the next orthographic viewport, cycling through plan and elevation views without reaching for the mouse. A small navigation convenience for multi-viewport work.

commands.name: NextPerspectiveViewport
commands.description: Switches focus to the next perspective viewport in the model. Useful when several perspective views are open for different camera studies.

commands.name: NextU
commands.description: Moves the control-point selection to the neighbouring point in the surface's U direction. Keyboard-friendly navigation for precise point editing on dense grids.

commands.name: NextV
commands.description: Moves the control-point selection to the neighbouring point in the surface's V direction. Pairs with NextU for stepping through a surface's point grid.

commands.name: NextViewport
commands.description: Makes the next viewport active, cycling through them in order. Quick keyboard navigation between views.

commands.name: NextViewportToTop
commands.description: Makes the next viewport active and brings it to the front. Useful when floating viewports overlap and the one you want is buried.

commands.name: NoEcho
commands.description: Stops commands echoing their text output to the command history. Used inside scripts and macros to keep the command line quiet while they run.

commands.name: NonmanifoldMerge
commands.description: Merges surfaces and polysurfaces into a single non-manifold polysurface, keeping shared internal faces rather than discarding them. Used in analysis and fabrication workflows where internal partitions matter.

commands.name: Notes
commands.description: Opens a simple text panel stored inside the model file. Useful for issue notes, modelling conventions and handover instructions that travel with the file.

commands.name: Notifications
commands.description: Opens the Notifications panel, which collects messages about updates, licensing and other events. Check it when the notification icon lights up.

commands.name: Offset
commands.description: Creates a parallel copy of a curve at a set distance, with corner and cap options. The backbone of wall thicknesses, clearance zones and repeated profile lines.

commands.name: OffsetCrvOnSrf
commands.description: Offsets a curve that lies on a surface so the copy stays on the surface at a true geodesic-style distance. Used for setting out seams and edge details on curved facades.

commands.name: OffsetMesh
commands.description: Offsets a mesh by a distance, optionally closing the result into a solid. The mesh equivalent of shelling, often used to give scanned or exported geometry a printable thickness.

commands.name: OffsetMultiple
commands.description: Offsets several curves at once by the same distance. Saves repeating Offset curve by curve when producing wall thicknesses or path edges across a drawing.

commands.name: OffsetNormal
commands.description: Offsets a curve that lies on a surface in the direction normal to that surface. Useful for building ribs, fins or upstands off doubly curved surfaces where a flat offset would be wrong.

commands.name: OffsetSrf
commands.description: Creates a copy of a surface or polysurface at a set distance along its normals, optionally building a closed solid between the two. The standard way to give architectural surfaces material thickness.

commands.name: OffsetSubD
commands.description: Offsets a SubD inwards or outwards, optionally building a closed solid shell between the two. The standard way to give sculpted skins a real material thickness.

commands.name: OneLayerOff
commands.description: Turns off the layer of an object you pick. A one-click declutter tool when you can see the offending geometry but do not know its layer name.

commands.name: OneLayerOn
commands.description: Turns on a single chosen layer and switches every other layer off. Instant focus when auditing one system, such as structure only.

commands.name: OneView
commands.description: Runs a single-viewport mode that swaps the construction plane automatically as you orbit near standard directions. A drafting-friendly way to work in one big view.

commands.name: Open
commands.description: Opens a Rhino model or any of the many supported CAD and mesh formats. Alongside Import, the gateway for consultant and manufacturer files.

commands.name: Options
commands.description: Opens Rhino's global settings for display, toolbars, aliases, modelling aids and more. Where you tune the environment to your own working style.

commands.name: OptionsExport
commands.description: Saves Rhino's options and settings out to a file. Use it to back up your setup or share office-standard settings across machines.

commands.name: OptionsImport
commands.description: Loads Rhino options and settings from a previously exported file. The other half of moving a familiar setup onto a new machine or standardising a team.

commands.name: OptionsPage
commands.description: Opens the Options dialog directly at a named page. Mainly used in toolbar buttons and macros that jump straight to a specific setting.

commands.name: Orient
commands.description: Moves, rotates and optionally scales objects by mapping two reference points onto two targets. A compound transform that places elements in one action instead of three.

commands.name: Orient3Pt
commands.description: Repositions objects by matching three reference points to three targets, fixing position and orientation in space. The reliable way to place a component onto a sloping plane.

commands.name: OrientCameraToSrf
commands.description: Aims the viewport camera perpendicular to a picked surface, looking straight at it. The quickest way to get a true face-on view of an angled facade or panel.

commands.name: OrientCrvToEdge
commands.description: Copies or moves a curve onto a surface edge, orienting it to match the edge. Handy for placing profile curves ready for sweeps along an edge.

commands.name: OrientOnCrv
commands.description: Places objects along a curve, orienting each to the curve direction. Useful for positioning individual elements like bollards where regular array spacing will not do.

commands.name: OrientOnSrf
commands.description: Places copies of an object onto a surface, aligned to the surface normal at each pick. Great for scattering rooflights or fixings across curved geometry by eye.

commands.name: Ortho
commands.description: Toggles constraint of cursor movement to set angle increments, typically 90 degrees. Fundamental drafting aid for keeping lines square.

commands.name: OrthoAngle
commands.description: Changes the angle that Ortho constrains to, which is 90 degrees by default. Set it to 30 or 45 degrees when working on angled grids or chamfered plans.

commands.name: OrthoSnapToCPlaneZ
commands.description: Toggles whether Ortho also constrains movement vertically along the construction plane's Z axis. Turn it on to draw and drag straight up and down while modelling in 3D.

commands.name: Osnap
commands.description: Opens the object snap controls for end, mid, centre, intersection and other precise picks. Accurate modelling in Rhino lives and dies by these snaps.

commands.name: PackageManager
commands.description: Browses, installs and updates plug-ins and resources from the official package server. The modern route to extending Rhino with tools like section utilities and renderers.

commands.name: Pan
commands.description: Slides the view across the model without changing zoom or angle. Basic navigation alongside Zoom and view rotation.

commands.name: Parabola
commands.description: Draws a parabola from focus or vertex definitions. Occasionally needed for reflector geometry, arch profiles and structural form studies.

commands.name: Paraboloid
commands.description: Draws a paraboloid surface, optionally capped into a solid. Useful for dish, reflector and canopy-style forms with true parabolic geometry.

commands.name: Paste
commands.description: Places clipboard contents into the model at their original coordinates. Completes the cut and copy clipboard workflow across files.

commands.name: PasteAsBlock
commands.description: Pastes the clipboard contents as a block instance rather than loose geometry. Useful for keeping repeated pasted elements lightweight and centrally editable.

commands.name: PasteAt
commands.description: Pastes the clipboard contents at a point you pick rather than at its original coordinates. Saves a paste-then-move step when bringing geometry between files.

commands.name: Patch
commands.description: Fits an approximate surface over a loose collection of curves, points or edges. A pragmatic hole-filler and terrain-builder when inputs are messy or incomplete.

commands.name: Pause
commands.description: A macro helper that pauses the macro for one user input, such as a pick or a value. The basic building block for interactive command macros.

commands.name: PerspectiveAngle
commands.description: Sets the lens angle of the perspective viewport's camera. Widen it for tight interior views, narrow it for flattering exterior shots with less distortion.

commands.name: PerspectiveMatch
commands.description: Matches the perspective camera to a background photograph by picking corresponding points, so the model lines up with the image. The key tool for dropping a proposal into a site photo.

commands.name: Picture
commands.description: Places an image in the model as a picture plane, commonly used to trace scanned drawings or display reference imagery. Successor to the old PictureFrame command.

commands.name: Pipe
commands.description: Wraps a solid circular section along any curve, with optional varying radii and caps. The fastest way to model handrails, service runs and structural tubes.

commands.name: PlaceHole
commands.description: Cuts a round hole into a planar face of a solid, with control over depth and direction. Faster and more deliberate than boolean-subtracting a cylinder by hand.

commands.name: Plan
commands.description: Sets the viewport to look straight down at the current construction plane. Instant return to true plan after working in 3D.

commands.name: Planar
commands.description: Toggles Planar mode, which keeps successive picks at the same construction-plane elevation as the previous point. Keeps 3D polylines and curves flat without constant elevator snapping.

commands.name: PlanarDifference
commands.description: Boolean-subtracts coplanar closed regions from one another, returning the trimmed 2D result. A drafting-style boolean for cleaning up overlapping outlines and hatch regions.

commands.name: PlanarIntersection
commands.description: Keeps only the overlapping area of coplanar closed regions, discarding the rest. Useful for finding the common footprint of stacked plan outlines.

commands.name: PlanarMesh
commands.description: Fills planar closed curves with a flat mesh, the mesh equivalent of PlanarSrf. Quick floors, panels and grounds for mesh-based scenes.

commands.name: PlanarSrf
commands.description: Creates flat surfaces from closed planar curves, including nested boundaries with holes. Everyday tool for turning plan outlines into floor plates and panels.

commands.name: PlanarUnion
commands.description: Merges coplanar closed regions into combined outlines, dissolving their overlaps. Good for consolidating overlapping plan shapes into a single boundary.

commands.name: Plane
commands.description: Draws a rectangular flat surface from corner to corner, with options for centre-out and three-point placement. The fastest way to make a ground plane, wall panel or backdrop.

commands.name: PlaneThroughPt
commands.description: Fits a rectangular plane through a set of points, averaging their positions. Useful for establishing a best-fit datum through surveyed or scanned data.

commands.name: PlayAnimation
commands.description: Plays back the animation set up with Rhino's animation tools, such as a turntable or sun study, in the viewport. Preview the motion before committing to recording frames.

commands.name: PlugInManager
commands.description: Lists installed plug-ins and lets you load, disable or install them. The place to go when a plug-in's commands stop appearing.

commands.name: Point
commands.description: Places a single point object at a picked or typed location. Useful for marking setting-out positions, snap targets and survey coordinates before drawing geometry.

commands.name: PointCloud
commands.description: Gathers selected point objects into a single point cloud, or breaks a cloud back into points. Keeps large scan or survey datasets manageable as one selectable object.

commands.name: PointCloudSection
commands.description: Cuts section profiles through a point cloud with a plane, extracting the points or polyline along the cut. The bridge from raw scan data to usable plan and section linework.

commands.name: PointDeviation
commands.description: Measures and colour-codes how far a set of points sits from a surface or mesh. Used to verify a rebuilt surface against original scan data.

commands.name: PointGrid
commands.description: Creates a rectangular grid of point objects. Useful as a scaffold for paving setouts, facade studies or anything needing a regular array of reference points.

commands.name: Points
commands.description: Places a run of point objects one after another until you press Enter. Quicker than repeating Point when plotting several markers or imported coordinate positions.

commands.name: PointsOff
commands.description: Hides control points when direct editing is finished. Prevents accidental dragging of points while working nearby.

commands.name: PointsOn
commands.description: Displays the control points of curves and surfaces so they can be dragged directly. The doorway into hands-on NURBS editing.

commands.name: Polygon
commands.description: Draws a regular polygon with any number of sides, inscribed or circumscribed about a radius. Handy for bolt patterns, kiosks and faceted plan forms.

commands.name: PolygonCount
commands.description: Reports how many render-mesh polygons the selection or scene contains. A quick weight check before exporting to real-time engines or worrying about display performance.

commands.name: Polyline
commands.description: Draws a connected chain of straight segments as one curve. Ideal for plan outlines, boundaries and any profile made of straight runs.

commands.name: PolylineOnMesh
commands.description: Draws a polyline whose points are constrained to a mesh surface. Ideal for sketching routes, paths or cut lines over scanned terrain.

commands.name: PopupMenu
commands.description: Opens the customisable pop-up command menu at the cursor, usually bound to the middle mouse button. Keeps favourite commands one click away without hunting through toolbars.

commands.name: PopupPopular
commands.description: Pops up a menu of your most-used commands at the cursor. A self-updating shortcut list based on how you actually work.

commands.name: PopupToolbar
commands.description: Pops up a chosen toolbar at the cursor for a quick pick, after which it disappears. Gives access to a whole toolbar without permanently docking it.

commands.name: PrevDetail
commands.description: Activates the previous detail on the current layout. Pairs with NextDetail for cycling through a sheet's views.

commands.name: PrevU
commands.description: Moves the control-point selection to the previous point in the surface's U direction. Part of the keyboard navigation set for precise point editing.

commands.name: PrevV
commands.description: Moves the control-point selection to the previous point in the surface's V direction. Part of the keyboard navigation set for precise point editing.

commands.name: PrevViewport
commands.description: Makes the previous viewport active, cycling backwards through them. The reverse of NextViewport.

commands.name: Print
commands.description: Sends layouts or viewports to a printer or PDF with scale, line width and colour controls. The final step in issuing drawings from Rhino.

commands.name: PrintDisplay
commands.description: Previews print output in the viewport, showing lineweights and print colours as they will plot. Check drawings with this on before sending anything to print.

commands.name: Project
commands.description: Projects curves or points straight down (or along a view direction) onto surfaces, polysurfaces or meshes. Used to push plan linework onto terrain or facade geometry.

commands.name: ProjectToCPlane
commands.description: Squashes objects flat onto the construction plane, optionally keeping the originals. Instantly turns 3D linework into a true 2D plan underlay.

commands.name: Properties
commands.description: Opens the panel showing the selected object's layer, colour, material and type-specific settings. The everyday place to check and adjust what something is.

commands.name: PropertiesPage
commands.description: Opens the Properties panel directly at a named page. Like OptionsPage, it exists mainly for toolbar buttons and macros that jump straight to a setting.

commands.name: Pull
commands.description: Pulls curves or points onto a surface by the shortest path rather than a fixed direction. Better than Project on steep or doubly curved surfaces where projection would distort placement.

commands.name: Purge
commands.description: Deletes unused layers, blocks, materials and other invisible data bloating the file. Often reclaims dramatic file size on long-running project models.

commands.name: PushPull
commands.description: Drags planar regions directly in or out to add or remove material, SketchUp-style. Introduced in Rhino 8, it makes fast massing edits without explicit boolean commands.

commands.name: PushViewportToBack
commands.description: Sends the active viewport behind the others in the stacking order. Useful for shuffling overlapping floating viewports.

commands.name: Pyramid
commands.description: Creates a solid pyramid with any number of base sides. Instant geometry for pyramidal roofs, skylights and obelisks.

commands.name: QuadrangulateMesh
commands.description: Merges pairs of triangles into quads where they lie close to planar. Tidies triangulated meshes into cleaner, lighter topology.

commands.name: QuadRemesh
commands.description: Rebuilds any mesh, surface or SubD as a clean quad-dominant mesh, optionally converting straight to SubD. Transforms scan data and faceted models into sculptable, well-flowing geometry.

commands.name: Radiate
commands.description: Applies live radial symmetry to a SubD so edits repeat around an axis. Added in Rhino 8 for rotationally patterned objects like lighting pieces and radial pavilions.

commands.name: Radius
commands.description: Reports the radius of a curve at a picked point. Quick verification that curved elements meet minimum bend or turning radii.

commands.name: RailRevolve
commands.description: Revolves a profile around an axis while its outer edge follows a rail curve, so the radius varies as it turns. Useful for shells and vault-like forms that are not purely circular in plan.

commands.name: ReadCommandFile
commands.description: Runs a plain text file of Rhino commands line by line. Simple batch automation without writing a proper script.

commands.name: ReadEveryIGESEntity
commands.description: An import troubleshooting toggle that forces Rhino to read every entity in an IGES file, including types normally skipped. Try it when an IGES import appears to be missing geometry.

commands.name: ReadViewportsFromFile
commands.description: Loads the viewport arrangement and views saved in another model file. Useful for standardising view setups across project files.

commands.name: Rebuild
commands.description: Reconstructs curves or surfaces with a chosen degree and control point count, evening out their structure. Standard clean-up before matching, deforming or exporting geometry.

commands.name: RebuildCrvNonUniform
commands.description: Refits a curve with non-uniformly spaced control points to a tolerance, placing fewer points on straight runs and more where the curve bends. Often gives cleaner results than plain Rebuild on mixed geometry.

commands.name: RebuildEdges
commands.description: Restores surface edges to their exact original positions after they have been forced by JoinEdge or drifted out of tolerance. A repair step when edge gaps start causing downstream failures.

commands.name: RebuildMeshNormals
commands.description: Recalculates a mesh's normals from its face geometry, discarding any custom vertex normals. The usual fix for odd shading on imported meshes.

commands.name: RebuildUV
commands.description: Rebuilds a surface in just the U or V direction with a chosen point count. Useful for evening out isocurve distribution in one direction while leaving the other intact.

commands.name: RecordAnimation
commands.description: Renders each frame of the set-up animation out to image files. The production step after previewing with PlayAnimation, ready for assembling into video.

commands.name: Rectangle
commands.description: Draws a rectangular polyline from two corners, a centre, or three points, with a rounded-corner option. The starting point for most plan footprints and panel outlines.

commands.name: Redo
commands.description: Reinstates the last change that Undo reversed. Handy when you step back one change too far.

commands.name: RedoMultiple
commands.description: Redoes several undone steps in one go. The counterpart to UndoMultiple for stepping back and forth through model history quickly.

commands.name: RedoView
commands.description: Re-applies a view change undone with UndoView. Lets you step forward again through camera history without re-navigating.

commands.name: ReduceMesh
commands.description: Lowers a mesh's polygon count while preserving its shape as far as possible. Essential for taming scan data and dense downloads before they slow the model.

commands.name: ReducePolyline
commands.description: Removes vertices from a polyline while keeping it within a tolerance of the original. Simplifies dense traced or imported polylines into manageable geometry.

commands.name: RefitTrim
commands.description: Refits a trimmed surface so a trimmed edge becomes a natural untrimmed edge. Valuable in continuity work, where matching and merging need untrimmed edges to succeed.

commands.name: Reflect
commands.description: Maintains a live mirrored half of a SubD so edits on one side update the other instantly. Invaluable for symmetrical furniture, vehicles and pavilion forms.

commands.name: RefreshAllTextures
commands.description: Reloads every texture image from disk, picking up edits made outside Rhino. Use it after tweaking a texture in an image editor so the viewport catches up.

commands.name: RefreshShade
commands.description: Discards and regenerates the display meshes of selected objects. The go-to fix when shaded surfaces look faceted, torn or out of date.

commands.name: ReleaseFromCage
commands.description: Disconnects objects from their cage-edit control object, freezing them in their current deformed shape. Do this once a cage deformation is final.

commands.name: RemapCPlane
commands.description: Re-orients objects from one construction plane to another, as if the geometry were drawn on the new plane. Excellent for moving 2D details onto sloped or vertical faces.

commands.name: RememberCopyOptions
commands.description: Toggles whether transform commands remember your last Copy yes/no choice between uses. Set it to suit whether you usually move or usually duplicate.

commands.name: RemoveControlPoint
commands.description: Deletes control points from a curve, or a whole row from a surface, letting the shape relax accordingly. Used to simplify over-defined geometry.

commands.name: RemoveCrease
commands.description: Returns creased SubD edges or vertices to smooth. Used when a hard edge should melt back into the surrounding form.

commands.name: RemoveFromGroup
commands.description: Takes selected objects out of their group while leaving the rest grouped. Useful for promoting one element out of a set for separate treatment.

commands.name: RemoveGuide
commands.description: Deletes guide lines placed with AddGuide. Keeps the infinite construction guides tidy once setting-out is done.

commands.name: RemoveKnot
commands.description: Deletes a knot from a curve or surface, simplifying its control structure with a slight shape change. Used to lighten over-detailed geometry before matching or exporting.

commands.name: RemoveMappingChannel
commands.description: Deletes a texture-mapping channel from the selected objects. Cleans up mapping setups that have accumulated unused channels.

commands.name: RemoveMultiKnot
commands.description: Removes stacked multiple knots from curves and surfaces, restoring smooth continuity where kinks were held. An advanced clean-up for geometry destined for high-quality surfacing.

commands.name: RemovePerFaceColors
commands.description: Strips per-face display colours from meshes and SubDs, returning them to their object colour. Undoes face-painting used during design studies.

commands.name: RemoveSymmetry
commands.description: Removes the symmetry constraint from a SubD so its mirrored halves can be edited independently. Use it once a symmetric form needs asymmetric refinement.

commands.name: Render
commands.description: Renders the current view with the active renderer into the render window. The starting point for presentation images beyond viewport captures.

commands.name: RenderAssignMaterialToLayer
commands.description: Assigns a render material to chosen layers so everything on them inherits it. The layer-based approach that keeps large models' materials manageable.

commands.name: RenderAssignMaterialToLayersOfObjects
commands.description: Assigns a render material to the layers that the selected objects sit on. A shortcut for layer-based materials when it is easier to pick objects than layer names.

commands.name: RenderAssignMaterialToObjects
commands.description: Assigns a render material directly to the selected objects, overriding their layer material. Use it for one-off material changes on individual elements.

commands.name: RenderBlowup
commands.description: Renders a picked region of the viewport enlarged, giving a high-resolution look at part of the frame. Useful for inspecting a detail without rendering the whole image at huge size.

commands.name: Rendering
commands.description: Opens the Rendering panel with the current renderer's settings, including resolution, quality and lighting options. Set things up here before pressing Render.

commands.name: RenderInWindow
commands.description: Renders only a rectangle of the view that you drag out. Saves time when you are iterating on one part of an image.

commands.name: RenderMergeIdenticalMaterials
commands.description: Merges duplicate identical render materials in the document into one. Declutters material lists bloated by imports and copy-pasting between files.

commands.name: RenderOpenLastRendering
commands.description: Reopens the most recent rendering saved with the file in the render window. Handy for revisiting the last result without re-rendering.

commands.name: RenderOpenRenderImage
commands.description: Opens a saved render image file in Rhino's render window, where post-effects and adjustments are available. Lets you revisit and tweak older renders.

commands.name: RenderPreview
commands.description: Renders the current view at draft quality for a fast check of composition, lighting and materials. Iterate here before committing to a full-quality render.

commands.name: RenderPreviewInWindow
commands.description: Renders a selected region of the view at draft quality. The quickest possible feedback loop when tuning one area of an image.

commands.name: RenderPreviewWindow
commands.description: Runs a draft-quality render in the render window. A quicker stand-in for Render while a scene is still evolving.

commands.name: RenderReportImageFiles
commands.description: Lists all the image and texture files the document references. Useful for auditing linked assets before archiving or sending a file to someone else.

commands.name: RenderReportMissingImageFiles
commands.description: Lists referenced texture and image files that cannot be found on disk. The first step in fixing renders full of missing-texture pink.

commands.name: RenderWindow
commands.description: Opens the render window showing the most recent render. Where render results live, along with save and post-effect options.

commands.name: RepairSubD
commands.description: Checks a SubD object for damaged or invalid structure and attempts to fix it. Reach for it when a SubD starts misbehaving after heavy editing or import.

commands.name: Reparameterize
commands.description: Changes the parameter domain of a curve or surface, for example to a 0-to-1 range, without altering its shape. Mostly matters for scripting, texture flow and flow-along-surface operations.

commands.name: ReplaceBlock
commands.description: Swaps selected block instances over to a different block definition. Perfect for replacing placeholder components, such as swapping massing trees for detailed ones.

commands.name: Rescue3dmFile
commands.description: Attempts to salvage geometry from a damaged or corrupt 3dm file. A last-resort recovery tool when a model will not open normally.

commands.name: Reset
commands.description: Restores Rhino's settings and window arrangement towards factory defaults. A troubleshooting reset for when the interface or behaviour has become unrecognisable.

commands.name: ResetMessageBoxes
commands.description: Re-enables warning dialogs previously dismissed with a do-not-show-again tick. Useful when a suppressed warning turns out to have mattered.

commands.name: Restore
commands.description: Restores the Rhino application window from a maximised or minimised state to its previous size and position. A window-management helper, mainly for scripts.

commands.name: RevCloud
commands.description: Draws a revision cloud around areas of change on a drawing. Added in Rhino 8 to support standard drawing issue and mark-up conventions.

commands.name: Revert
commands.description: Abandons unsaved changes and reloads the file from disk. The emergency exit after an experiment goes wrong beyond comfortable undoing.

commands.name: Revolve
commands.description: Spins a profile curve around an axis to create a surface of revolution. The fastest route to domes, columns, bowls and other rotationally symmetrical forms.

commands.name: RevolvedHole
commands.description: Cuts a hole with a revolved custom profile into a solid, ideal for countersinks, counterbores and chamfered recesses. More control than a plain round hole.

commands.name: Rib
commands.description: Adds a rib, a thin stiffening slab grown from a curve, onto a solid. A product-design feature tool that also suits fins and brackets in fabrication models.

commands.name: Ribbon
commands.description: Creates a ribbon: it offsets a curve and builds the surface between the curve and its offset. An instant flat strip for paths, borders and edging.

commands.name: RibbonOffset
commands.description: Offsets a curve while automatically resolving self-intersections, then builds a clean ribbon surface between curve and offset. Much more reliable than plain Offset around tight, complex outlines.

commands.name: Rotate
commands.description: Rotates objects around a centre point within the construction plane. Constant companion for orienting plans, furniture and site elements.

commands.name: Rotate3D
commands.description: Rotates objects around an axis you define by two points in space. Needed whenever the rotation is out of the construction plane, like tilting a roof panel.

commands.name: RotateCamera
commands.description: Swivels the camera in place, like turning your head rather than orbiting the model. Useful for interior views where the eye position must stay fixed.

commands.name: RotateHole
commands.description: Rotates an existing hole feature on a solid face to a new orientation without re-cutting it. Part of Rhino's hole-editing family alongside move and mirror.

commands.name: RotateView
commands.description: Orbits the camera around the view target. The keyboard-driven counterpart to right-mouse orbiting in perspective views.

commands.name: RoundHole
commands.description: Cuts a circular hole into a solid at a picked point, with depth and direction options. Faster than drawing a cylinder and boolean-subtracting for fixings and service penetrations.

commands.name: Run
commands.description: Launches an external program from within Rhino. Occasionally useful in scripted pipelines that hand files to other software.

commands.name: RunPythonScript
commands.description: Runs a Python script file, Rhino's main door to Python automation. The command behind most custom toolbar buttons that do clever things.

commands.name: RunScript
commands.description: Runs RhinoScript code or a script file. The classic automation route on Windows Rhino, predating the Python tools.

commands.name: Save
commands.description: Saves the current model, including its render meshes and previews. Frequent saving plus IncrementalSave is cheap insurance on live projects.

commands.name: SaveACopy
commands.description: Saves the current model to a new file while you carry on working in the original. Perfect for milestone snapshots and issuing versions without switching files.

commands.name: SaveAs
commands.description: Saves the model under a new name, location or earlier Rhino version. Also the route to handing files to consultants on older releases.

commands.name: SaveAsTemplate
commands.description: Saves the current file as a template, preserving its units, layers, annotation styles and settings for new projects. Build one good template and every project starts properly set up.

commands.name: SaveRenderWindowAs
commands.description: Saves the image in the render window to a file such as PNG or JPEG. The final step of getting a render out of Rhino and into a presentation.

commands.name: SaveSmall
commands.description: Saves without render meshes to produce a much smaller file. Standard practice before emailing or archiving large models.

commands.name: SaveWindowLayout
commands.description: Saves the current arrangement of panels and toolbars as a named window layout. Switch between task-specific setups, such as modelling versus drafting, in one step.

commands.name: Scale
commands.description: Resizes objects uniformly in all directions from an origin, by factor or reference distance. Used to correct imported drawing scales and resize elements proportionally.

commands.name: Scale1D
commands.description: Stretches objects along a single direction only. Ideal for lengthening a table, corridor or facade bay without changing its other proportions.

commands.name: Scale2D
commands.description: Scales objects in two directions while holding the third. Useful for resizing plans in plan-only without altering heights.

commands.name: ScaleEach
commands.description: Scales every selected object individually about its own base point, rather than the whole selection about one origin. Resize a field of repeated elements in place without them drifting apart.

commands.name: ScaleNU
commands.description: Scales objects by independent factors along X, Y and Z. The tool for squashing or stretching massing studies non-uniformly.

commands.name: ScalePositions
commands.description: Scales the distances between selected objects without resizing the objects themselves. Spread out or gather an arrangement, such as a furniture layout, while every piece keeps its size.

commands.name: ScaleTextHeight
commands.description: Scales the text height of selected annotations by a factor. The quick fix when notes and dimensions turn out the wrong size for the drawing scale.

commands.name: ScreenCaptureToClipboard
commands.description: Captures the active viewport, as displayed on screen, to the clipboard. The fastest route from model to email or slide deck.

commands.name: ScreenCaptureToFile
commands.description: Captures the active viewport, as displayed on screen, straight to an image file. Good for quick record shots without setting up a render.

commands.name: ScriptEditor
commands.description: Opens Rhino's script editor for writing, debugging and running Python and C# code. The modern home for automation, introduced alongside Rhino 8's scripting overhaul.

commands.name: Section
commands.description: Creates section curves where a picked plane slices through objects. Quick one-off cuts for studying profiles or extracting a single section line for drawings.

commands.name: SectionStyles
commands.description: Controls how clipped geometry displays at the cut, including hatch, fill and edge styling per object or layer. Part of the Rhino 8 sectioning workflow for drawing-quality live sections.

commands.name: SelAll
commands.description: Selects every visible, unlocked object in the model. Common first step before bulk transforms, exports or clean-ups.

commands.name: SelAnnotationStyle
commands.description: Selects all annotations that use a given annotation style. Ideal for auditing drawings or updating every note in one style at once.

commands.name: SelBadObjects
commands.description: Selects every invalid object in the model in one command. Pairs with Check to locate and repair or replace corrupt geometry.

commands.name: SelBlockInstance
commands.description: Selects block instances in the model. Useful before block-wide operations such as replacing or counting components.

commands.name: SelBlockInstanceNamed
commands.description: Selects every instance of a specific block definition by name. The quick way to grab all copies of one component, such as a particular window type.

commands.name: SelBoundary
commands.description: Selects objects using a closed boundary curve you pick as the selection region. Lets a drawn outline, such as a site boundary, do the selecting for you.

commands.name: SelBrush
commands.description: Selects objects by painting over them with a draggable brush. A natural fit for picking through cluttered areas where window selections grab too much.

commands.name: SelBrushPoints
commands.description: Selects control points by painting over them with a brush. Invaluable in sculpting workflows on dense point grids and SubD control cages.

commands.name: SelCaptives
commands.description: Selects every object currently captured by a control object, such as a cage created with CageEdit. Useful for checking which geometry is still being deformed by a cage before you edit or release it.

commands.name: SelChain
commands.description: Selects a run of curves or edges connected end to end from one pick. Speeds up choosing rails and boundaries for sweeps, lofts and fillets.

commands.name: SelChildren
commands.description: Adds the history children of the current selection - the objects that were built from it and update when it changes. Reach for it when you need everything that depends on a parent curve or surface.

commands.name: SelCircular
commands.description: Selects objects by dragging a circular region in the viewport rather than the usual rectangular window, with window or crossing behaviour. Handy for grabbing everything around a point, such as a column and its fittings.

commands.name: SelClippingPlane
commands.description: Selects all clipping plane objects in the model. Clipping planes are often hard to pick amongst dense geometry, so this gathers them in one go for moving, hiding or deleting.

commands.name: SelClippingPlaneInViewport
commands.description: Selects only the clipping planes that affect the active viewport. Useful in models where different views carry different section cuts and you want to adjust just the ones cutting the current view.

commands.name: SelClosedCrv
commands.description: Selects all closed curves in the model in one go. Handy when preparing profiles for extrusion or checking which outlines are ready to become surfaces.

commands.name: SelClosedMesh
commands.description: Selects all closed, watertight meshes - the ones ready for 3D printing or Boolean work. A quick audit before export.

commands.name: SelClosedPolysrf
commands.description: Selects every closed polysurface - that is, watertight solids. Useful for auditing a model before Boolean operations, sectioning or volume calculations.

commands.name: SelClosedSrf
commands.description: Selects all closed single surfaces, such as spheres and tori. Pairs with SelOpenSrf when sorting a model by what is sealed and what is not.

commands.name: SelClosedSubD
commands.description: Selects all closed SubD objects - those with no open edges. Handy when checking which SubD forms are watertight before converting or printing.

commands.name: SelColor
commands.description: Selects all objects displaying a chosen colour. Useful for rounding up imports whose colours came in by object rather than layer.

commands.name: SelConnected
commands.description: Grows a sub-object selection on a mesh or SubD to include everything topologically connected to it. Saves laborious clicking when you need a whole region of faces or edges.

commands.name: SelConnectedMeshFaces
commands.description: From a picked face, selects all the mesh faces joined to it. Useful for grabbing one shell of a mesh that actually contains several disjoint pieces.

commands.name: SelControls
commands.description: Selects the control objects, such as CageEdit cages, that are deforming other geometry. Pairs with SelCaptives when tidying up or removing cage-editing set-ups.

commands.name: SelCrossing
commands.description: Runs a crossing selection: drag a window and anything the rectangle touches is selected, not only what sits fully inside. The explicit command form is mainly useful in macros and scripts.

commands.name: SelCrv
commands.description: Selects all curve objects in one hit. Ideal for bulk operations like moving construction linework to its own layer.

commands.name: SelDetail
commands.description: Selects detail viewports on the active layout. Handy when a detail's border is hard to pick, or you want every detail at once before locking them against accidental panning.

commands.name: SelDim
commands.description: Selects every dimension in the model. A quick way to gather annotation for moving to a dedicated layer, restyling or purging.

commands.name: SelDimAngular
commands.description: Selects all angular dimensions, leaving other annotation alone. Useful when a drawing's angle callouts need restyling or checking as a set.

commands.name: SelDimCentermark
commands.description: Selects all centre-mark annotations - the cross marks placed at circle and arc centres - so they can be restyled or tidied as a set.

commands.name: SelDimLinear
commands.description: Selects all linear and aligned dimensions in one go, so a drawing's main measurements can be restyled or moved together.

commands.name: SelDimOrdinate
commands.description: Selects all ordinate dimensions - the datum-based callouts used on fabrication drawings - so they can be managed as a set.

commands.name: SelDimOverride
commands.description: Selects dimensions whose annotation-style settings have been overridden on the object. Useful for auditing drawings where individual dimensions have drifted from the document standard.

commands.name: SelDimRadial
commands.description: Selects all radius and diameter dimensions, handy when circular callouts need checking or restyling across a drawing.

commands.name: SelDimTextOverride
commands.description: Selects dimensions whose displayed text has been typed over rather than showing the true measured value. Well worth running before issuing drawings, so faked figures do not slip through.

commands.name: SelDot
commands.description: Selects all annotation dots - the screen-facing labels that keep a constant size. Useful for restyling or clearing markers scattered through a model.

commands.name: SelDup
commands.description: Selects objects that are exact duplicates sitting on top of others. The classic pre-delete step for cleaning files bloated by double geometry.

commands.name: SelDupAll
commands.description: Selects all duplicate objects including the originals, unlike SelDup which leaves one copy of each unselected. Use it to review a duplication problem before deciding what to keep.

commands.name: Select
commands.description: Command-line object selection: prompts you to pick objects and adds them to the current selection. Mostly used inside macros and scripts where an explicit selection step is needed.

commands.name: SelectionFilter
commands.description: Opens the selection filter control, which limits picking to chosen object types such as curves, surfaces or annotation. Invaluable in dense models where clicks keep landing on the wrong thing.

commands.name: SelectionFilterEdges
commands.description: Sets the selection filter so that picks grab edge sub-objects of surfaces, meshes and SubDs without holding Ctrl+Shift. Turn it off again once the edge work is done.

commands.name: SelectionFilterEnable
commands.description: Switches the selection filter on or off without changing its settings - a quick escape when the filter is blocking normal picking.

commands.name: SelectionFilterFaces
commands.description: Sets the selection filter so that picks grab face sub-objects, useful for repeated face-level editing on SubDs, meshes and polysurfaces.

commands.name: SelectionFilterNone
commands.description: Clears every tick in the selection filter so nothing can be picked - mainly used at the start of macros before enabling only the types wanted.

commands.name: SelectionFilterToggle
commands.description: Toggles the selection filter between enabled and disabled while keeping its current settings, so you can flip in and out of filtered picking quickly.

commands.name: SelectionFilterVertices
commands.description: Sets the selection filter so that picks grab vertex and control-point sub-objects - useful for stretches of point-level editing on meshes and SubDs.

commands.name: SelEdgeLoop
commands.description: From one picked edge, selects the whole edge loop running across a mesh or SubD. Essential in SubD modelling for creasing, deleting or transforming a complete feature line at once.

commands.name: SelEdgeRing
commands.description: Selects an edge ring - the parallel edges marching around a mesh or SubD - from a single pick. Complements SelEdgeLoop when harvesting topology for editing.

commands.name: SelExtrusion
commands.description: Selects all lightweight extrusion objects in the model. Useful when you need to convert them to polysurfaces for editing, or to see what UseExtrusions has been creating.

commands.name: SelFaceLoop
commands.description: Selects a run of faces forming a loop across a SubD or mesh from one picked face - quick material for extruding, colouring or deleting a whole strip.

commands.name: SelFacesToBoundary
commands.description: Grows a face selection on a SubD or mesh outwards until it reaches a boundary such as creases, open edges or selected edges - a fast way to fill a bounded region of faces.

commands.name: SelFence
commands.description: Selects by drawing a freehand fence line through the model; anything the line crosses is selected. Good for picking a scattered string of objects in one stroke.

commands.name: SelFontUse
commands.description: Selects the text and annotation that use a particular font. Useful when standardising drawings, or hunting down notes set in the wrong typeface after a file swap.

commands.name: SelGroup
commands.description: Selects a group by choosing its name from a list - a lifesaver when groups are buried in a crowded model or sit off screen.

commands.name: SelHatch
commands.description: Selects every hatch in the model, useful for moving all fills to their own layer or adjusting them after a drawing revision.

commands.name: SelHatchPattern
commands.description: Selects all hatches that use a specified pattern - for example, to swap every brick hatch for a different style in one edit.

commands.name: SelID
commands.description: Selects an object by typing or pasting its unique identifier (GUID). Mostly a scripting and troubleshooting tool - for instance, chasing down an object reported by an audit command.

commands.name: SelLast
commands.description: Reselects the objects changed or created by the most recent command. Invaluable for chaining operations, like moving what you just imported.

commands.name: SelLayer
commands.description: Selects every object on layers you choose. Combines with hide, export or transform commands for layer-wide operations.

commands.name: SelLayerNumber
commands.description: Selects everything on a layer identified by its position number in the layer list. Largely a legacy and scripting convenience - most people select by layer name instead.

commands.name: SelLeader
commands.description: Selects all leaders - the arrowed annotation callouts - so they can be restyled, re-layered or purged together.

commands.name: SelLight
commands.description: Selects all light objects - spotlights, point lights, rectangular lights and the rest - which are often awkward to click in a busy scene.

commands.name: SelLine
commands.description: Selects all straight line curves, ignoring arcs and freeform curves. Handy when cleaning up imported CAD linework or isolating construction lines.

commands.name: SelLinetype
commands.description: Selects objects drawn with a given linetype - useful when reorganising imported drawings where dashed, chain and continuous lines carry different meanings.

commands.name: SelMappingWidget
commands.description: Selects texture-mapping widgets - the box, sphere or plane gizmos that control how textures wrap objects - so you can move or scale them. They are easy to lose track of in the viewport.

commands.name: SelMaterialName
commands.description: Selects every object that uses a particular material, chosen by name. A quick way to audit or re-assign materials across a scene before rendering.

commands.name: SelMesh
commands.description: Selects all mesh objects. Convenient for isolating imported context meshes from native NURBS work.

commands.name: SelMeshEdges
commands.description: Selects mesh edge sub-objects, gathering edges so operations such as extraction, welding or creasing can act on them directly.

commands.name: SelMeshFacesByArea
commands.description: Selects mesh faces whose area falls within a range you set. Great for finding sliver faces in scan data or exports before repairing or deleting them.

commands.name: SelMeshFacesByAspectRatio
commands.description: Selects mesh faces by their aspect ratio, flagging the long thin faces that cause shading artefacts and analysis problems. A useful triage step on meshes destined for rendering or simulation.

commands.name: SelMeshFacesByDraftAngle
commands.description: Selects mesh faces whose draft angle relative to a pull direction falls within a set range. Useful when checking mouldability, CNC tool access or overhangs for 3D printing on mesh models.

commands.name: SelMeshFacesByEdgeLength
commands.description: Selects mesh faces with edges longer or shorter than limits you set, helping to locate over-coarse patches or degenerate slivers in a mesh.

commands.name: SelMeshPart
commands.description: Selects one connected piece of a mesh that contains several disjoint parts - pick a face and the whole part highlights, ready to split off or delete. Common when dissecting scan meshes.

commands.name: SelMirroredBlocks
commands.description: Selects block instances that have been mirrored (negatively scaled). Worth running before export or fabrication, as mirrored blocks can misbehave in other applications.

commands.name: SelNakedMeshEdgePt
commands.description: Selects the mesh vertices lying on naked, unjoined edges, showing exactly where a mesh fails to close. Follow up with welding or edge-matching tools to shut the gaps before printing.

commands.name: SelName
