commands.description: Selects objects by their assigned object name. Depends on disciplined naming, but then gives instant pinpoint selection in large files.

commands.name: SelNamedViewWidget
commands.description: Selects named-view widgets - the camera markers displayed in the model for saved views - so they can be moved, hidden or deleted.

commands.name: SelNone
commands.description: Clears the current selection entirely. Useful in scripts and when Escape is mapped elsewhere.

commands.name: SelNonManifold
commands.description: Selects non-manifold edges, where more than two faces meet along one edge - a defect that breaks 3D printing and Boolean operations. Use it alongside ZoomNonManifold to inspect each problem spot.

commands.name: SelObjectsWithHistory
commands.description: Selects every object carrying construction history, so you can see what will update when parent geometry changes - or purge history before sending a file out.

commands.name: SelOpenCrv
commands.description: Selects all open curves - the ones that fail to close into loops. The usual first step when hunting gaps in linework destined for extrusion or planar surfaces.

commands.name: SelOpenMesh
commands.description: Selects all meshes with naked edges - the ones not yet watertight. A quick audit before 3D printing or Boolean work.

commands.name: SelOpenPolysrf
commands.description: Selects every open polysurface - joined surfaces that do not seal into a solid. Run it before Booleans or volume calculations to find the leaky models.

commands.name: SelOpenSrf
commands.description: Selects all open single surfaces, complementing SelClosedSrf when sorting a model by what is sealed and what is not.

commands.name: SelOpenSubD
commands.description: Selects all SubD objects with open edges - the unfinished or deliberately open forms - so they can be reviewed or closed up.

commands.name: SelParents
commands.description: Adds the history parents of the current selection - the input geometry that drives it. Useful for finding which curve to edit when you want a lofted or extruded surface to update.

commands.name: SelPicture
commands.description: Selects all picture objects - reference images placed with the Picture command - which tend to hide behind geometry and resist picking.

commands.name: SelPlanarCrv
commands.description: Selects all curves that lie flat in a plane - the ones eligible for PlanarSrf, hatching or clean extrusion. Anything left unselected probably has a stray point off-plane.

commands.name: SelPlanarSrf
commands.description: Selects all planar surfaces - flat faces such as floor plates and panels - which is useful before flattening, hatching or replacing them with simpler geometry.

commands.name: SelPolyline
commands.description: Selects all polylines - curves made purely of straight segments - handy for isolating imported CAD linework or set-out geometry from freeform curves.

commands.name: SelPolysrf
commands.description: Selects all polysurfaces, including closed solids. Quick filter when exporting or re-layering built massing.

commands.name: SelPrev
commands.description: Restores the previous selection set. A lifesaver after accidentally deselecting a painstaking multi-pick.

commands.name: SelPt
commands.description: Selects every point object. Typical use is deleting leftover setting-out or divide points before issuing a model.

commands.name: SelPtCloud
commands.description: Selects all point cloud objects, which are otherwise fiddly to pick amongst geometry. Useful when managing survey and scan data alongside a model.

commands.name: SelRectangular
commands.description: Rectangular region selection as an explicit command, with window and crossing options - chiefly useful inside macros where the selection method must be spelt out.

commands.name: SelRenderColor
commands.description: Selects objects whose render colour matches one you specify - a way of grouping geometry by colour in models where materials were assigned loosely.

commands.name: SelSelfIntersectingCrv
commands.description: Selects curves that cross themselves. Self-intersections wreck offsets, extrusions and planar surfaces, so this is a key clean-up check on imported or traced linework.

commands.name: SelShortCrv
commands.description: Selects curves shorter than a length you give - the classic way to find the stray slivers left behind by exploding, importing or aggressive trimming.

commands.name: SelSmall
commands.description: Selects objects smaller than a size you give. Excellent for catching slivers and debris left over from trims and imports.

commands.name: SelSrf
commands.description: Selects every single-surface object in the model. Useful for separating unjoined surfaces from finished polysurfaces during clean-ups.

commands.name: SelSubD
commands.description: Selects all SubD objects in the model. Useful when converting or re-layering sculpted concept geometry en masse.

commands.name: SelSubDEdges
commands.description: Selects SubD edge sub-objects, gathering edges ready for creasing, bevelling or transforming without picking them one by one.

commands.name: SelSubDFriendlyCrv
commands.description: Selects curves that are SubD-friendly - degree 3 with uniform structure - and therefore behave well as inputs to SubD tools. Anything unselected may need MakeSubDFriendly first.

commands.name: SelText
commands.description: Selects all text objects in the model, useful for restyling notes, moving them to an annotation layer or checking fonts across a drawing set.

commands.name: SelTrimmedSrf
commands.description: Selects all trimmed surfaces - those whose underlying surface has been cut back by trims. Useful before shrinking, untrimming or checking a model for export.

commands.name: SelU
commands.description: With control points on, selects an entire row of points running in the surface's U direction from a single pick - far faster than window-selecting rows when sculpting surfaces.

commands.name: SelUntrimmedSrf
commands.description: Selects all untrimmed surfaces - full four-sided sheets with no cuts - complementing SelTrimmedSrf when auditing how a model was built.

commands.name: SelUV
commands.description: Selects the crossing rows of control points in both the U and V directions through a picked point, giving a cross-shaped selection for symmetrical surface editing.

commands.name: SelV
commands.description: With control points on, selects an entire row of points running in the surface's V direction from a single pick - the partner to SelU for fast row-based surface editing.

commands.name: SelVisible
commands.description: Selects only the objects actually visible in the current viewport, ignoring geometry hidden behind other objects in shaded views. Good for grabbing exactly what a client sees in a particular view.

commands.name: SelVolumeObject
commands.description: Selects objects inside or crossing a closed solid you pick - selection by real 3D volume rather than a screen window. Useful for harvesting everything within a massing volume or zone.

commands.name: SelVolumePipe
commands.description: Selects objects inside an imaginary pipe along a curve - for example, everything within a set distance of a route, cable run or road centreline.

commands.name: SelVolumeSphere
commands.description: Selects objects inside a sphere you define by centre and radius - a true three-dimensional radius search around a point in the model.

commands.name: SelWindow
commands.description: Window selection as an explicit command: only objects entirely inside the dragged rectangle are selected. Mainly for macros and scripts that need the method spelt out.

commands.name: SendBackward
commands.description: Moves the selected object one step back in the draw order, changing how overlapping curves, hatches and pictures stack on screen and in prints. Draw order matters most in 2D drawing and presentation work.

commands.name: SendToBack
commands.description: Sends the selected object to the very back of the draw order, so everything else displays and prints on top of it - the usual treatment for background images and fills.

commands.name: SetActiveViewport
commands.description: Makes a named viewport the active one from the command line - a scripting and macro building block rather than something you would type by hand.

commands.name: SetCurrentRenderPlugIn
commands.description: Chooses which installed render engine - Rhino Render or a third-party renderer - the Render command and render tools drive. Switch here when a project moves between quick previews and production rendering.

commands.name: SetDimensionLayer
commands.description: Nominates a layer that new dimensions and annotation land on automatically, keeping drawing notes off your modelling layers without constant layer switching.

commands.name: SetDisplayMode
commands.description: Switches the viewport between display modes such as Wireframe, Shaded, Rendered, Ghosted, Arctic and Raytraced. Different modes suit drafting, design review and presentation checking.

commands.name: SetDocumentUserText
commands.description: Attaches key-value text data to the document itself - job numbers, revision notes, project metadata - which scripts, Grasshopper and title-block fields can read back.

commands.name: SetFlythroughAnimation
commands.description: Sets up a fly-through animation in which the camera travels along a path curve you choose, and Rhino records the frames. The classic way to walk a client through a scheme.

commands.name: SetGroupName
commands.description: Renames an existing group so it can be found and selected by a meaningful name later - worth doing as models grow and 'Group01' stops meaning anything.

commands.name: SetIgesLayerLevelMap
commands.description: Controls how Rhino layers map to level numbers when exchanging IGES files - needed when a receiving CAD system expects a particular level convention.

commands.name: SetLayerLinetype
commands.description: Assigns a linetype to a layer from the command line, so everything on that layer inherits it - the scriptable counterpart to setting it in the Layers panel.

commands.name: SetLayerToObject
commands.description: Makes the current layer whichever layer a picked object sits on - a very quick way to start drawing on the same layer as existing work without opening the Layers panel.

commands.name: SetLinetype
commands.description: Applies a linetype to the selected objects, overriding what their layer would give them - dashed for demolition, chain for centrelines and so on.

commands.name: SetLinetypeScale
commands.description: Sets the global scale factor applied to linetype patterns, so dashes and chains read correctly at your model units and print scales.

commands.name: SetMaximizedViewport
commands.description: Maximises a named viewport so it fills the graphics area - mainly used in scripts and toolbar macros to jump straight to a particular working view.

commands.name: SetObjectDisplayMode
commands.description: Overrides the display mode of selected objects in a viewport - for instance keeping context buildings wireframe while your proposal shows rendered. One of the best tricks for readable working views and illustrative screenshots.

commands.name: SetObjectName
commands.description: Gives the selected object a name, visible in Properties and usable by selection and reporting tools - the foundation of tidy, searchable models.

commands.name: SetOneDaySunAnimation
commands.description: Creates a sun-study animation across a single day: Rhino steps the sun through its positions for a chosen date and location and records the frames. Ideal for shadow studies supporting planning applications.

commands.name: SetOrtho
commands.description: Turns ortho mode on or off from the command line, constraining cursor movement to set angles - the scriptable twin of the status bar's Ortho pane.

commands.name: SetPathAnimation
commands.description: Animates the camera along a path curve while it aims at a target you define, then records the frames - more controllable than a freehand fly-through for rehearsed presentation routes.

commands.name: SetPerFaceColorByFacePack
commands.description: Colours each face pack of a SubD with its own flat colour, making visible how faces will group together when the object converts to NURBS. A diagnostic aid for judging SubD topology.

commands.name: SetPlanar
commands.description: Toggles planar mode, which keeps successively picked points at the same construction-plane elevation - helpful when tracing plans or drawing flat linework in a 3D view.

commands.name: SetPt
commands.description: Flattens selected objects or control points to a shared X, Y or Z value. The classic tool for levelling points onto a datum, such as zeroing survey linework to Z0.

commands.name: SetRedrawOff
commands.description: Suspends viewport redrawing so scripts and macros run without screen flicker and repaint slowdowns. Pair it with SetRedrawOn when the script finishes.

commands.name: SetRedrawOn
commands.description: Restores viewport redrawing after SetRedrawOff, refreshing the screen so you can see the results of a script's work.

commands.name: SetSeasonalSunAnimation
commands.description: Creates a sun study across the year, animating the sun's position at a fixed time of day through the seasons - useful for solstice-to-solstice shadow and daylight comparisons.

commands.name: SetSnap
commands.description: Sets the grid snap spacing and toggles grid snap from the command line - useful in scripts and when setting up drafting-style precision for orthogonal work.

commands.name: SetSpotlightToView
commands.description: Moves the selected spotlight so it shines from the current viewport's camera position: aim the view where you want light, run the command, and the light matches it.

commands.name: SetTurntableAnimation
commands.description: Sets up a turntable animation in which the camera orbits around the model (or the model appears to spin), recording the frames. The standard product-shot style presentation of an object or massing model.

commands.name: SetUserText
commands.description: Attaches key-value text data to selected objects - door numbers, finishes, cost codes - which the Properties panel, scripts and Grasshopper can read back. The lightweight route to data-rich models.

commands.name: SetView
commands.description: Points the viewport at a standard direction such as Top, Front, Right or Perspective, in world or CPlane terms. The command behind the standard view buttons.

commands.name: SetViewFocusDistance
commands.description: Sets the camera's focus distance for the active view, which depth-of-field effects in raytraced display and rendering use to decide what appears sharp.

commands.name: SetViewToSpotlight
commands.description: Points the active viewport's camera to match a spotlight, so you see exactly what the light covers - invaluable when aiming accent lighting in interiors.

commands.name: SetWorkingFolder
commands.description: Sets the default folder Rhino uses when opening and saving files - a small tidy-up that keeps project files landing in the right place during a long session.

commands.name: SetZoomExtentsBorder
commands.description: Adjusts how much breathing space Zoom Extents leaves around the model, as a scale factor. Set it once if you find extents zooms habitually too tight or too loose.

commands.name: Shade
commands.description: Temporarily displays the viewport shaded regardless of its display mode. A quick look at form and shadow while staying in wireframe workflows.

commands.name: ShadeSelected
commands.description: Displays a temporary shaded preview of just the selected objects while everything else stays wireframe - a quick look at form without changing display modes.

commands.name: Shear
commands.description: Slants objects at an angle while keeping their base fixed. Used for leaning facades, italic-style extrusions and racking studies.

commands.name: Shell
commands.description: Hollows a closed solid to a set wall thickness, removing the faces you pick as openings. Ideal for turning massing volumes into thin-walled enclosures in one move.

commands.name: ShortPath
commands.description: Draws the shortest path (geodesic) curve across a surface between two points - the route a taut string would take over the form. Useful for seam lines, panelling set-out and edge details on doubly curved surfaces.

commands.name: Show
commands.description: Reveals all hidden objects at once. The blanket undo for a session's worth of hiding.

commands.name: ShowDir
commands.description: Displays direction and normal arrows on curves and surfaces persistently while you carry on working, unlike Dir's temporary display. Turn the arrows off with ShowDirOff.

commands.name: ShowDirOff
commands.description: Turns off the persistent direction arrows displayed by ShowDir once you have finished checking curve directions and surface normals.

commands.name: ShowEdges
commands.description: Highlights the edges of surfaces and meshes, with naked and non-manifold edges picked out in colour. The go-to diagnostic when a join fails or a solid will not close.

commands.name: ShowEdgesOff
commands.description: Turns off the edge highlighting left by ShowEdges once you have finished hunting naked and non-manifold edges.

commands.name: ShowEnds
commands.description: Marks the ends of open curves on screen so stray gaps in linework stand out - a great companion when tidying drawings into closed profiles for surfacing or hatching.

commands.name: ShowEndsOff
commands.description: Turns off the curve-end markers displayed by ShowEnds when the linework clean-up is done.

commands.name: ShowInDetail
commands.description: Reveals objects that were hidden in a particular layout detail, restoring per-detail visibility without affecting the model or other views.

commands.name: ShowLayersInDetail
commands.description: Turns layers back on inside a chosen detail after they were hidden there, letting each drawing view on a layout carry its own layer set.

commands.name: ShowOsnap
commands.description: Opens the object snap control so you can tick which snaps - end, mid, centre and the rest - are live while you model.

commands.name: ShowRenderMesh
commands.description: Displays the render mesh that shading and rendering use to approximate NURBS objects, so you can judge whether the mesh is fine enough before rendering or export.

commands.name: ShowSelected
commands.description: Temporarily displays hidden objects so you can pick which ones to reveal, leaving the rest hidden. Precision control when only some hidden items should return.

commands.name: ShowSelectedInDetail
commands.description: Shows chosen hidden objects in the active detail only, giving precise per-view control over what each drawing on a layout displays.

commands.name: ShowToolbar
commands.description: Shows a toolbar you name, restoring it after it was closed - the companion to HideToolbar in workspace-arranging macros.

commands.name: ShowZBuffer
commands.description: Displays the viewport's depth buffer as a greyscale image, with distance from the camera mapped to tone. Occasionally handy for producing depth maps used in post-production and illustration.

commands.name: ShrinkTrimmedSrf
commands.description: Shrinks the hidden underlying surface of a trimmed face so it sits closely around the trim boundary. Good housekeeping before matching, exporting or editing control points.

commands.name: ShrinkTrimmedSrfToEdge
commands.description: Shrinks a trimmed surface's underlying surface right up to a selected trim edge, cutting away the invisible excess sheet beyond the trims. A finer-grained variant of ShrinkTrimmedSrf.

commands.name: ShrinkWrap
commands.description: Wraps a watertight mesh tightly around any collection of geometry, meshes or point clouds. A Rhino 8 favourite for turning messy scans and mixed models into a single printable solid mesh.

commands.name: Silhouette
commands.description: Extracts outline curves of objects as seen from the current view or a set direction. Useful for shadow studies, elevational outlines and preparing artwork from 3D models.

commands.name: SimplifyCrv
commands.description: Replaces segments of a polycurve with true lines and arcs where possible, reducing clutter. Excellent for cleaning up curves imported from CAD drawings.

commands.name: SingleSubDFace
commands.description: Creates one standalone SubD face from picked corner points. The seed for box-modelling a form face by face with AppendFace.

commands.name: Sketch
commands.description: Draws a freehand curve that follows the dragged cursor, optionally on a surface or mesh. Handy for loose concept lines and annotating models during design reviews.

commands.name: Slab
commands.description: Offsets a planar curve and extrudes the result into a solid with thickness and height in one step. A quick way to raise walls from single plan lines.

commands.name: Smash
commands.description: Roughly flattens a surface that is only slightly doubly curved, ignoring small distortions. A quick-and-dirty alternative to Squish for near-developable panels.

commands.name: Smooth
commands.description: Averages out control point positions to relax curves, surfaces or meshes, with per-axis control. Good for calming noisy traced linework or lumpy meshes.

commands.name: Snap
commands.description: Toggles grid snap, making the cursor jump to grid intersections - the command behind the status bar's Snap pane. Useful for quick orthogonal set-out at regular spacings.

commands.name: Snapshots
commands.description: Saves named states combining view, layer visibility, object states and more, with animated transitions between them. Powerful for presenting design options and phasing from one model.

commands.name: SnapSize
commands.description: Sets the grid snap spacing - the distance between the invisible points the cursor jumps to when Snap is on. Match it to your planning grid or module.

commands.name: SnapToLocked
commands.description: Toggles whether object snaps engage locked objects. Turn it on to draw accurately over a locked survey or base drawing without risk of moving it.

commands.name: SnapToMeshObject
commands.description: Toggles whether object snaps find points on mesh objects - switch it off when heavy scan meshes keep hijacking snaps meant for your NURBS model.

commands.name: SnapToOccluded
commands.description: Toggles snapping to geometry hidden behind other objects in shaded views. Off means you only snap to what you can see; on lets you reach through the model to covered points.

commands.name: SnapToSubDObject
commands.description: Toggles whether object snaps engage SubD objects, letting you decide if snaps should land on smooth SubD forms while drawing around them.

commands.name: SoftEditCrv
commands.description: Drags a point on a curve while nearby regions follow with a smooth falloff. Ideal for nudging long design curves without introducing kinks or editing individual control points.

commands.name: SoftEditSrf
commands.description: Drags a point on a surface with a smooth circular falloff so the surrounding region follows naturally. Ideal for sculpting gentle bumps and hollows into terrain or shell forms.

commands.name: SoftMove
commands.description: Moves geometry or control points with a smooth falloff from a centre, like a soft magnet. Useful for organic nudges to terrain and sculpted surfaces.

commands.name: SoftTransform
commands.description: Moves, rotates or scales a selection with a smooth falloff, so nearby control points or sub-objects follow progressively less. Sculpting-style editing for SubDs, meshes and dense control-point grids.

commands.name: SolidPtOn
commands.description: Turns on grip points at the corners and edges of a solid so they can be dragged directly. A light-touch way to deform boxes and simple polysurfaces without exploding them.

commands.name: Sphere
commands.description: Creates a solid sphere from centre and radius or other constructions. Used for domes, finials and quick volumetric placeholders.

commands.name: SphereTangentToThreeSurfaces
commands.description: Draws a sphere tangent to three chosen surfaces - a specialist construction useful for fillet set-outs, packing studies and finding the ball that just fits a corner.

commands.name: Spiral
commands.description: Draws a flat or conical spiral with controllable turns and radii. Useful for ramps, spiral geometry studies and decorative patterns.

commands.name: Split
commands.description: Divides objects into pieces where cutters cross them, keeping every part. Preferred over Trim when you want to recolour, move or keep both sides of a cut.

commands.name: SplitDisjointMesh
commands.description: Breaks a mesh containing unconnected pieces into separate mesh objects. The bulk version of ExtractMeshPart for cleaning imported models.

commands.name: SplitEdge
commands.description: Splits a surface or polysurface edge at points you pick, so the resulting edge segments can be joined, matched or blended independently. MergeEdge reverses it.

commands.name: SplitFace
commands.description: Divides a planar face of a solid along a curve or between points without breaking the solid apart. Sets up sub-faces that MoveFace or PushPull can then manipulate independently.

commands.name: SplitMeshEdge
commands.description: Splits a mesh edge at a point, adding a vertex and dividing the neighbouring faces - low-level mesh surgery for adding local detail or fixing awkward triangulation.

commands.name: SplitMeshWithCurve
commands.description: Splits a mesh along a curve projected onto it - the standard way to cut panel lines, site boundaries or trim edges into scan and terrain meshes.

commands.name: SplitPointCloud
commands.description: Splits a point cloud into separate clouds, letting you carve a large scan into manageable chunks - one cloud per building, floor or zone.

commands.name: SplitViewportHorizontal
commands.description: Splits the active viewport into two stacked views, giving you an extra viewport without rebuilding the whole layout - useful for a quick plan-over-perspective pairing.

commands.name: SplitViewportVertical
commands.description: Splits the active viewport into two side-by-side views - a fast way to work in two views at once without switching to a four-view layout.

commands.name: Splop
commands.description: Copies and morphs an object from a plane onto a surface at picked points, with rotate and scale control while placing. Fun and fast for stamping repeated ornaments over curved forms.

commands.name: Sporph
commands.description: Morphs objects from one surface's parameter space to another's, deforming them between the two shapes. Used to migrate detailed geometry between design iterations of a surface.

commands.name: Squish
commands.description: Flattens doubly curved surfaces or meshes by allowing controlled stretching and compression, and can report the distortion. Used to pattern fabric panels, upholstery and stretch ceilings.

commands.name: SquishBack
commands.description: Takes geometry drawn on a squished (flattened) surface and maps it back onto the original 3D form. Draw your pattern, graphics or cut lines flat, then return them to the curved surface.

commands.name: SquishInfo
commands.description: Reports how a squished object relates to its 3D original, including the flattening data that SquishBack relies on - a check that the link between flat and curved versions is intact.

commands.name: SrfControlPtGrid
commands.description: Creates a surface from a rectangular grid of points used as control points - the surface is smoothed and guided by the grid rather than passing through it. Useful for building clean freeform surfaces from set-out data.

commands.name: SrfPt
commands.description: Creates a surface by picking three or four corner points. Quick for simple planes and twisted quads such as warped roof panels.

commands.name: SrfPtGrid
commands.description: Creates a surface that passes through a rectangular grid of points - handy for rebuilding surveyed terrain or spreadsheet-derived surfaces where the points must be honoured exactly.

commands.name: SrfSeam
commands.description: Relocates the seam of a closed surface to a different isocurve position. Fixes texture, trim and matching issues that cluster around a badly placed seam.

commands.name: STEPTree
commands.description: Shows the assembly structure of a STEP file, so the product tree from an imported engineering model can be browsed and worked with rather than arriving as an anonymous heap of geometry.

commands.name: Stitch
commands.description: Zips selected SubD or mesh edges together so they become shared edges. The tool for closing gaps and welding sculpted parts into one continuous body.

commands.name: Stretch
commands.description: Elongates only the middle region of objects along an axis, leaving the ends undistorted. Ideal for lengthening a chair rail or window while keeping its end details intact.

commands.name: SubCrv
commands.description: Extracts the portion of a curve between two picked points, either shortening the original or copying just that stretch. Quicker than splitting and deleting when you only need part of a curve.

commands.name: SubDBox
commands.description: Creates a SubD box with a chosen number of faces per side. A common starting block for organic massing that will be sculpted by pushing points and edges.

commands.name: SubDCone
commands.description: Creates a SubD cone primitive for sculpting tapered organic shapes. Handy for tent-like and horn-like starting volumes.

commands.name: SubDCrease
commands.description: Makes selected SubD edges or vertices fully creased, so the smooth surface carries a sharp corner or arris there. The way to mix crisp architectural edges into otherwise soft SubD forms.

commands.name: SubDCylinder
commands.description: Creates a SubD cylinder with configurable face counts. A clean starting point for soft columns, trunks and limb-like forms.

commands.name: SubDDisplayToggle
commands.description: Switches SubD display between smooth and flat (boxy control cage) modes. Designers flip to flat mode for precise topology edits, then back to judge the smooth result.

commands.name: SubDEllipsoid
commands.description: Draws an ellipsoid as a SubD object, giving you a smooth stretched-sphere primitive ready for organic push-and-pull editing.

commands.name: SubDExpandEdges
commands.description: Expands selected SubD edges into narrow strips of faces, adding topology either side of a feature line so you can control how tightly the surface turns there.

commands.name: SubDFaceEdgeVertexToggle
commands.description: Cycles the sub-object selection filter between SubD faces, edges and vertices - usually run from a keyboard shortcut so you can flip picking modes mid-edit without leaving the viewport.

commands.name: Subdivide
commands.description: Splits selected SubD or mesh faces into smaller faces for denser local control. Used when one area of a sculpt needs much finer modelling than the rest.

commands.name: SubDLoft
commands.description: Lofts a series of profile curves into a SubD surface with clean quad flow. A Rhino 8 addition for building smooth sculptable skins straight from section curves.

commands.name: SubDPlane
commands.description: Creates a flat SubD plane divided into a grid of faces. The usual canvas for sculpting terrain-like or draped SubD surfaces.

commands.name: SubDSphere
commands.description: Creates a smooth SubD sphere built from quad faces. Useful as a base for organic forms like pods, boulders and soft furniture.

commands.name: SubDSpinEdge
commands.description: Rotates an interior SubD edge so it connects different corners of the neighbouring faces, rerouting topology without adding or removing points - useful for cleaning up awkward flow in a SubD mesh.

commands.name: SubDSweep1
commands.description: Sweeps profiles along one rail to produce a SubD rather than a NURBS surface. Keeps concept geometry light and editable for further sculpting.

commands.name: SubDSweep2
commands.description: Sweeps profiles along two rails to build a SubD skin controlled at both edges. Useful for organic canopies and seat shells that need later point editing.

commands.name: SubDTorus
commands.description: Creates a SubD ring primitive. A useful base for smooth loops, seating rings and continuous banded forms.

commands.name: SubDTruncatedCone
commands.description: Draws a truncated cone as a SubD object - a smooth frustum primitive for organic modelling, tapering columns and vessel-like forms.

commands.name: Sun
commands.description: Controls a sun light by date, time and location for accurate shadows. Essential for daylight and rights-of-light style studies directly in the viewport.

commands.name: SwapMeshEdge
commands.description: Flips the diagonal edge shared by two triangular mesh faces, changing how their quad is divided - a classic fix for ugly shading and creasing in triangulated meshes.

commands.name: SwapView
commands.description: Exchanges the view shown in the active viewport with that of another viewport - quick reshuffling of your workspace without redefining cameras.

commands.name: Sweep1
commands.description: Runs one or more cross-section shapes along a single rail curve to build a surface. Ideal for handrails, mouldings and extrusion-like forms that follow a curved path.

commands.name: Sweep2
commands.description: Builds a surface by carrying cross-sections along two rail curves, keeping both edges under control. The tool of choice when a shape must hit two defined boundary curves.

commands.name: Symmetry
commands.description: Mirrors a curve or SubD edge across a plane and keeps the join smooth, with history so edits stay symmetrical. Used for precise symmetrical design curves and SubD halves.

commands.name: SynchronizeCPlanes
commands.description: Applies the active viewport's construction plane to the other viewports, keeping CPlanes consistent while you work on a tilted or rotated plane across several views.

commands.name: SynchronizeRenderColors
commands.description: Brings render material colours and object display colours into line with each other, so shaded views and renders agree - useful for quick colour-coded massing and option studies.

commands.name: SystemInfo
commands.description: Prints a report of Rhino's version, graphics hardware and loaded plug-ins. The first thing support asks for when troubleshooting display or stability issues.

commands.name: Taper
commands.description: Scales an object progressively along an axis so it narrows or widens towards one end. Quick way to give massing a tapering silhouette.

commands.name: TCone
commands.description: Creates a truncated cone between two circular ends of different radii. Handy for tapered columns, hoppers and flared connections.

commands.name: Text
commands.description: Places a block of annotation text at a picked point, styled by the current annotation style. Used for titles, notes and labels throughout drawings.

commands.name: TextObject
commands.description: Generates real geometry from text as curves, surfaces or solids. Reach for it for signage, embossed lettering and CNC-cut graphics rather than annotation.

commands.name: TextProperties
commands.description: Opens the settings for selected text objects so their content, font and formatting can be changed - a direct route into text editing alongside the Properties panel.

commands.name: Textures
commands.description: Opens the Textures panel, where the image and procedural textures in the document are created and managed for use in materials, environments and decals.

commands.name: ThicknessAnalysis
commands.description: Colour-maps the wall thickness of closed solids or meshes between set limits. Valuable for checking shelled components and 3D print walls before fabrication.

commands.name: ThicknessAnalysisOff
commands.description: Turns off the false-colour thickness analysis display once you have finished checking wall thicknesses for printing or fabrication.

commands.name: TiltView
commands.description: Rolls the camera about its own axis, tilting the horizon of the view. Occasionally useful for dramatic perspectives, or for levelling a named view that has picked up an accidental tilt.

commands.name: ToggleFloatingViewport
commands.description: Floats the active viewport as its own window, or docks it back into the main layout - handy for throwing a perspective view onto a second monitor while drafting in the first.

commands.name: ToggleLeftSidebar
commands.description: Shows or hides the left sidebar of the Rhino window, freeing screen space for the viewports on smaller displays.

commands.name: ToggleRenderMesh
commands.description: Toggles display of objects' render meshes on and off - a quick way to inspect the mesh that sits behind shaded and rendered display.

commands.name: ToggleRightSidebar
commands.description: Shows or hides the right sidebar of the Rhino window - typically the Properties and panel stack - to give viewports more room.

commands.name: ToNURBS
commands.description: Converts SubD or mesh objects into NURBS surfaces and polysurfaces. Used when a sculpted concept needs precise trimming, filleting or export to documentation.

commands.name: ToolbarLock
commands.description: Locks the toolbar layout so buttons and toolbars cannot be dragged out of place by stray clicks - worth switching on once your workspace is arranged.

commands.name: Torus
commands.description: Creates a solid ring from a centre, ring radius and tube radius. Occasionally needed for handrail loops, gaskets and toroidal architectural forms.

commands.name: ToSubD
commands.description: Converts meshes, NURBS surfaces or extrusions into SubD objects. The gateway for bringing existing geometry into Rhino's smooth sculpting workflow.

commands.name: TriangulateMesh
commands.description: Splits all quad mesh faces into triangles. Required by some export formats and analysis tools that only accept triangulated geometry.

commands.name: TriangulateNonPlanarQuads
commands.description: Splits only the non-planar quad faces of a mesh into triangles, fixing the faces that some exporters and engines reject while leaving flat quads untouched.

commands.name: TriangulateRenderMeshes
commands.description: Triangulates the render meshes of selected objects, useful when a downstream renderer or file format cannot cope with quad faces.

commands.name: Trim
commands.description: Cuts away the parts of objects you click, using other objects as cutting edges. Together with Split and Join, the core editing operation in every Rhino session.

commands.name: TruncatedCone
commands.description: Draws a solid truncated cone - a cone with its top sliced off flat. The frustum primitive for tapered columns, hoppers, lampshades and planters.

commands.name: TruncatedPyramid
commands.description: Draws a solid truncated pyramid - a pyramid cut off flat before its apex. Useful for plinths, rooflights, pad foundations and battered walls.

commands.name: Tube
commands.description: Creates a hollow straight cylinder with wall thickness in one operation. Quicker than boolean-subtracting two cylinders for sleeves and ducts.

commands.name: Turntable
commands.description: Spins the model continuously in the viewport. A simple way to review a design from all sides or run an impromptu presentation loop.

commands.name: Tutorials
commands.description: Opens Rhino's tutorials panel, with guided lessons and sample files - a good signpost for newcomers finding their way around the program.

commands.name: TweenCurves
commands.description: Generates intermediate curves evenly blended between two input curves. Great for louvre arrays, contour infills and transitional profiles between two design conditions.

commands.name: TweenSurfaces
commands.description: Creates one or more surfaces evenly interpolated between two input surfaces - useful for louvre arrays, stepped facades and transitional forms that morph from one shape to another.

commands.name: Twist
commands.description: Rotates an object progressively along an axis so it spirals between start and end angles. The instant twisted-tower and helical-fin tool.

commands.name: Undo
commands.description: Steps back through recent commands, reversing changes to the model. The most pressed shortcut in any session.

commands.name: UndoMultiple
commands.description: Undoes several steps in one go by letting you choose how far back to unwind, instead of hammering Ctrl+Z and hoping.

commands.name: UndoSelection
commands.description: Restores the previous selection set - a rescue when a mis-click deselects the collection of objects you had carefully built up.

commands.name: UndoView
commands.description: Steps back through recent view changes without touching geometry. Rescues you after an accidental zoom or orbit loses a carefully framed view.

commands.name: Ungroup
commands.description: Dissolves the selected group back into independent objects. The exit route when grouped items need separate editing.

commands.name: UngroupAll
commands.description: Removes all levels of grouping from the selection in one go, where Ungroup only peels off the top level of nested groups.

commands.name: UnifyMeshNormals
commands.description: Flips inconsistent face normals so the whole mesh points one way. A standard repair before boolean operations, rendering or 3D printing.

commands.name: Unisolate
commands.description: Restores the objects hidden by the last Isolate. Returns the full model after focused work.

commands.name: UnisolateFromViewports
commands.description: Ends per-viewport isolation, bringing back objects that had been hidden in particular viewports so all views show the full model again.

commands.name: UnisolateLock
commands.description: Reverses IsolateLock, unlocking the objects that were locked so you could work on an isolated selection undisturbed.

commands.name: UnjoinEdge
commands.description: Un-joins edges that were force-joined with JoinEdge, restoring them as separate naked edges - a sensible first step before rebuilding a dubious joint properly.

commands.name: Unlock
commands.description: Releases all locked objects so they can be selected again. Blanket partner to Lock.

commands.name: UnlockSelected
commands.description: Lets you pick specific locked objects to release while others stay locked. Fine-grained partner to Unlock for busy reference-heavy files.

commands.name: UnpackTextures
commands.description: Saves the texture images embedded in the 3dm file out to a folder on disk, so they can be edited, replaced or shared separately from the model.

commands.name: UnrollSrf
commands.description: Flattens developable (single-curvature) surfaces onto a plane, with their marked curves and labels. Essential for fabrication drawings of sheet metal, timber veneers and curved cladding.

commands.name: Untrim
commands.description: Removes a trim boundary and restores the full underlying surface, optionally keeping the trimming curves. Used to recover clean geometry when a trim needs rethinking.

commands.name: UntrimAll
commands.description: Removes every trim from a surface, recovering the full underlying sheet - the fastest way to strip out holes and cut edges when you want to start the trimming again.

commands.name: UntrimBorder
commands.description: Removes only the outer trim boundary of a surface, restoring the full sheet while keeping any interior holes intact.

commands.name: UntrimHoles
commands.description: Removes the interior holes from a trimmed surface while keeping its outer boundary - ideal for blanking off openings before re-detailing a facade or panel.

commands.name: Unweld
commands.description: Splits mesh vertices along edges above a crease angle so those edges shade as sharp. Used to restore crisp arris lines on smoothed meshes.

commands.name: UnweldEdge
commands.description: Unwelds only the specific mesh edges you pick, making them shade as creases. Precise control over which lines read sharp in a rendered mesh.

commands.name: Unwrap
commands.description: Flattens an object's surface into UV texture space, using seam edges you choose, so textures can be applied or painted without stretching - the starting point for serious texture-mapping work.

commands.name: UseExtrusions
commands.description: Sets whether commands such as Box, Cylinder and ExtrudeCrv create lightweight extrusion objects or full polysurfaces. Extrusions keep big repetitive models fast; polysurfaces suit heavy downstream editing.

commands.name: UVEditor
commands.description: Opens the UV editor, which shows a flattened copy of the object's texture coordinates that you edit to control exactly how textures wrap the model.

commands.name: VariableBlendSrf
commands.description: Creates a smooth blend surface between edges with its size and shape varying along the run, controlled by handles - for transitions that need to swell and tighten along their length.

commands.name: VariableChamferSrf
commands.description: Chamfers between surfaces with distances that vary along the edge, set by handles - angled transitions that change width along their run.

commands.name: VariableFilletSrf
commands.description: Fillets between surfaces with a radius that varies along the edge, adjusted by handles - for fillets that need to grow or shrink along a run rather than stay constant.

commands.name: VariableOffsetSrf
commands.description: Offsets a surface with different distances at chosen points, blending smoothly between them. Useful when a shell or panel must thicken structurally in some zones only.

commands.name: ViewCaptureToClipboard
commands.description: Copies a viewport image straight to the clipboard for pasting into emails, decks and documents. The fastest route from model to meeting note.

commands.name: ViewCaptureToFile
commands.description: Saves an image of the viewport at chosen resolution, with options for grid and widget visibility. The workhorse for quick design-study images without full rendering.

commands.name: ViewFirstFrame
commands.description: Jumps the animation preview to its first frame, taking you back to the start of a recorded fly-through or sun study.

commands.name: ViewFrameNumber
commands.description: Jumps the animation preview to a frame number you type - useful for checking a specific moment in a fly-through or sun study without playing the whole sequence.

commands.name: ViewLastFrame
commands.description: Jumps the animation preview to its final frame - a quick check of how a fly-through or sun study ends.

commands.name: ViewNextFrame
commands.description: Steps the animation preview forward one frame, letting you inspect a camera path or sun study frame by frame.

commands.name: ViewportTabs
commands.description: Shows or hides the viewport tabs along the edge of the graphics area - the quick way to flip between viewports and layout pages.

commands.name: ViewPreviousFrame
commands.description: Steps the animation preview back one frame - the partner to ViewNextFrame when scrubbing through a recorded sequence.

commands.name: Volume
commands.description: Calculates the enclosed volume of closed solids or meshes. Key for cut-and-fill studies, concrete quantities and capacity checks.

commands.name: VolumeCentroid
commands.description: Finds the centre of mass of closed volumes and marks it with a point. Used in stability and rigging studies for heavy elements.

commands.name: VolumeMoments
commands.description: Calculates volume, centroid and moments of inertia for closed solids - engineering-grade mass-property data straight from the model, useful for structural and stability checks.

commands.name: Walkabout
commands.description: Moves the camera at eye level with walking-style controls. Handy for checking interior spatial experience without setting up a full walkthrough.

commands.name: WebBrowser
commands.description: Opens a simple web browser panel inside Rhino - occasionally useful for keeping reference pages, product data or web tools alongside the model.

commands.name: Weight
commands.description: Edits the weight of selected control points, changing how strongly they pull the curve or surface towards them - higher weights tighten the shape locally, lower weights slacken it. A rational-geometry tool for fine control.

commands.name: Weld
commands.description: Merges coincident mesh vertices within an angle tolerance so faces share smooth shading. Fixes faceted-looking seams on imported meshes.

commands.name: WeldEdge
commands.description: Welds the mesh vertices along chosen edges so the adjoining faces share them and shade smoothly across the join - targeted smoothing where Weld's angle-based approach is too blunt.

commands.name: WeldVertices
commands.description: Welds selected mesh vertices so the faces around them share single vertices, removing the shading splits at those points - handy for spot-fixing seams in a mesh.

commands.name: What
commands.description: Prints a detailed report of an object's type, structure and validity. First stop for identifying mystery geometry in inherited files.

commands.name: WindowLayout
commands.description: Saves and restores named arrangements of Rhino's windows, panels and toolbars - one layout for modelling, another for drafting, another for rendering, switched in a click.

commands.name: WireCut
commands.description: Slices a solid using a curve projected through it, keeping or discarding the pieces you choose. An intuitive cutter for stepped facades and profile-driven subtractions.

commands.name: Worksession
commands.description: Attaches other Rhino files as read-only references around your active file, so a team can split a big project into parts. Rhino's answer to external references for large-project collaboration.

commands.name: Zebra
commands.description: Projects stripe patterns onto surfaces so continuity flaws show as kinked or broken stripes. The quickest visual check of how smoothly surfaces meet.

commands.name: ZebraOff
commands.description: Turns off the zebra-stripe analysis display once you have finished checking surface smoothness and continuity.

commands.name: Zoom
commands.description: Zooms the viewport by window, extents, selected objects or factor. Its aliases make framing the whole model or a selection a two-keystroke habit.

commands.name: Zoom1To1Calibrate
commands.description: Calibrates your monitor by measuring a known distance on screen, so that Zoom 1To1 can display the model at true real-world size - useful for judging details and text at actual scale.

commands.name: ZoomLens
commands.description: Changes the active perspective view's lens length, zooming by focal length rather than moving the camera - wide angle for interiors, long lens for flatter, elevational-feeling perspectives.

commands.name: ZoomNaked
commands.description: Steps the view through each naked edge on the selected objects, zooming to them one by one so open joints can be inspected and repaired - the natural follow-up to ShowEdges.

commands.name: ZoomNonManifold
commands.description: Steps the view through each non-manifold edge on the selected objects, zooming to every spot where more than two faces meet an edge - the fastest way to inspect the defects that break printing and Booleans.
